  - id: feature13
    title: "Pack/Publish Refactor — Local Archive + Registry Publish Flow"
    description: |
      Refactor packaging and publishing responsibilities:
      - `kinnoo pack <agent-dir>` becomes the default archival mechanism and always stores
        versioned `.kno` artifacts under `~/.kinnoo/archive/<agent-name>/<version>/<agent-name>.kno`.
      - `kinnoo publish <agent-name>` becomes a registry publication workflow that reads the
        latest packaged archive from the local archive and publishes it to a registry target.

      For V1 of registry publishing, mock the online registry in-repo at:
      `registry-scratch/jerry/<agent-name>/<version>/<agent-name>.kno`

      `kinnoo publish` must prevent hard overwrite of an existing tagged version by
      archiving old content as `untagged-1`, `untagged-2`, etc., then storing the new
      payload at the requested tagged version path.
    tasks: [task80, task81, task82, task83, task84, task85, task86, task87, task88, task89, task90]
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "Running `kinnoo pack <agent-dir>` writes archive output to `~/.kinnoo/archive/<agent-name>/<version>/<agent-name>.kno` by default and no longer relies on ad-hoc output location as the primary path."
      - id: AC2
        description: "`kinnoo pack` output clearly prints archive destination path and packaged version (including existing `[kinnoo pack] Agent version: <version #>` message contract)."
      - id: AC3
        description: "If the target archive path already exists, `kinnoo pack` uses explicit overwrite confirmation behavior and preserves file on decline."
      - id: AC4
        description: "`kinnoo publish <agent-name>` resolves the latest version of `<agent-name>` from `~/.kinnoo/archive/<agent-name>/` and publishes that artifact (no manual archive path required)."
      - id: AC5
        description: "V1 publish target is local mock registry path `registry-scratch/jerry/<agent-name>/<version>/<agent-name>.kno` (login deferred)."
      - id: AC6
        description: "If the same tagged version already exists in publish target, prior artifact is preserved as `untagged-<n>` and the new artifact is written at the tagged version path."
      - id: AC7
        description: "`kinnoo publish` prints clear outcome messages including source archive path, target registry path, and any untagged rollover actions."
      - id: AC8
        description: "Clear errors are printed when source archive for `<agent-name>` is missing, when no versions exist, or when archive metadata is invalid."
      - id: AC9
        description: "Feature12 local-registry name-based install/list/search behavior is explicitly deprecated or isolated so responsibilities are unambiguous: archive management in pack, registry publication in publish."
      - id: AC10
        description: "`kinnoo install <name>` resolves the latest version from the mock registry and installs it; implementation is structured so switching to a real remote registry later is a minimal change."
      - id: AC11
        description: "`kinnoo install <name>==<version>` installs a specific version from the mock registry."
      - id: AC12
        description: "`kinnoo list` displays by default all locally archived agents with name, latest version, and description."
      - id: AC13
        description: "`kinnoo list --local` displays all locally archived agents with name, latest version, and description."
      - id: AC14
        description: "`kinnoo list --remote` displays all registry agents with name, latest version, and description, using the mock registry for now."
      - id: AC15
        description: "`kinnoo search <query>` filters by default the local archive by name/description substring match."
      - id: AC16
        description: "`kinnoo search --local <query>` filters the local archive by name/description substring match."
      - id: AC17
        description: "`kinnoo search --remote <query>` filters the remote registry by name/description substring match, using the mock registry for now."
      - id: AC18
        description: "`kinnoo install <file-path/file.kno>` (file path) continues to work as before (V1 behavior preserved)."
      - id: AC19
        description: "New source-mode CLI arguments (`--local`, `--remote`, selector forms) provide clear usage/help and deterministic errors for invalid combinations (e.g., conflicting flags, missing query/selector), with no ambiguous fallback behavior."
    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature5, feature8, feature11]
    status: completed

  - id: feature15
    title: "Trust Baseline"
    description: |
      Add transparency and trust features: display dependency/secret name summary on install,
      warn when installing agents from unverified sources, log run traces, and perform a
      heuristic code sweep for env var value exposure. Absolute rule: no env var or secret
      VALUES ever appear in output, logs, or code paths — only names.
    tasks: [task98, task99, task100, task101, task102, task103, task104]
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "`kinnoo install` displays a summary of what the agent requires (env_var NAMES, dependency NAMES, runtime type) before installing and prompts for yes/no confirmation. A `--yes` (`-y`) flag skips the confirmation prompt for CI/automation pipelines."
      - id: AC2
        description: "If an agent is installed from a raw .kno file (not from a registry or archive) without an accompanying checksum .kno.sha256 file, a confirmation prompt is asked before proceeding: 'This agent is from an unverified source. Continue? (y/n)'."
      - id: AC3
        description: "`kinnoo run` logs a trace in JSON format to ~/.kinnoo/logs/run.<TIMESTAMP>.log containing ONLY: timestamp, agent name, agent version, runtime type, and exit code — no input content, no env var values, no secrets."
      - id: AC4
        description: "Log file never contains actual values of environment variables, secrets, or user input."
      - id: AC5
        description: "All trust-related display and logging code includes inline comments documenting the 'no secret values' invariant."
      - id: AC6
        description: "`kinnoo inspect` includes a heuristic security sweep of all .py files in the agent directory (excluding .venv/) that detects patterns where env var values may be printed, logged, or written to files. Warnings are displayed with file path and line number. A clean scan prints 'Security sweep: no env var exposure patterns detected (heuristic)'. The sweep also runs during `kinnoo pack` as a non-blocking warning before archiving."
    notes:
      - "Original AC4 (first-run display of env/dep names) was dropped — redundant with kinnoo inspect and kinnoo run --preflight."
      - "AC6 is a regex-based heuristic, not taint analysis. Output includes a disclaimer about false positives."
      - "--yes/-y flag on install follows apt/brew convention for CI automation."
    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature10]
    status: completed

  - id: feature18
    title: "Input Safety Guard"
    description: |
      Add a pluggable input safety check to `kinnoo run` that inspects user-provided input
      for common injection patterns (SQL injection, shell command injection, path traversal,
      SSRF, XSS, template injection) before passing it to the agent entrypoint. The guard is
      non-blocking — it warns and prompts for confirmation rather than hard-rejecting input.
      The architecture uses a Protocol-based design so the V1 regex guard can be swapped for
      an ML-based classifier in the future without changing callers.

      The guard is designed to work with both the current single-string input model
      (`kinnoo run <path> "<input>"`) and a future parameterized input model
      (`kinnoo run <path> -e <string> -i <id> -d <file-path> -u <url>`). For parameterized
      inputs, the guard applies type-aware pattern filtering: file path inputs emphasize path
      traversal detection, URL inputs emphasize SSRF detection, ID inputs enforce stricter
      injection patterns. A `check_inputs()` multi-value method accepts typed parameters so
      callers can pass all inputs in a single call and receive an aggregated result.
    tasks: [task116, task117, task118, task119, task120]
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "`kinnoo run` checks user input against injection patterns (SQL injection, shell command injection, path traversal, SSRF, XSS, template injection) before executing the agent entrypoint."
      - id: AC2
        description: "When a pattern match is found, a warning is printed to stderr listing the detected threat(s), and the user is prompted with 'Proceed anyway? [y/N]'. Answering 'n' or empty aborts with non-zero exit. Answering 'y' proceeds normally. Non-interactive stdin (no TTY) auto-aborts as a fail-safe."
      - id: AC3
        description: "A `--no-guard` flag on `kinnoo run` disables the input safety check entirely for CI/automation pipelines where input is controlled."
      - id: AC4
        description: "The guard implementation follows a Protocol-based pluggable design (`InputGuard` protocol with `check(value, input_type) -> InputGuardResult` and `check_inputs(inputs) -> InputGuardResult`) so the regex-based guard can be replaced with an ML-based guard via a single factory function change."
      - id: AC5
        description: "Each regex pattern in the V1 guard is individually unit-testable and documented with the threat category it detects."
      - id: AC6
        description: "Legitimate agent input that happens to resemble injection (e.g., a database agent receiving SQL) is not hard-blocked — the user can always proceed after the warning."
      - id: AC7
        description: "The guard supports type-aware input checking: 'text' (full scan), 'file_path' (path traversal + shell injection), 'url' (SSRF + shell injection), 'id' (SQL + shell + template injection), enabling future parameterized input modes (-e, -i, -d, -u) without code changes."
      - id: AC8
        description: "A `check_inputs()` method accepts a list of (param_name, value, input_type) tuples and returns an aggregated result with per-parameter warnings, ready for future multi-parameter input."
    notes:
      - "V1 uses RegexInputGuard with patterns for 6 threat categories: SQL injection (UNION SELECT, DROP TABLE, tautology, comment injection, WAITFOR DELAY), shell injection (;&| with dangerous commands, $() and backtick substitution, pipe to shell), path traversal (../, encoded variants, absolute sensitive paths), SSRF (file://, gopher://, dict://, internal IPs, AWS metadata 169.254.169.254), XSS (<script, javascript:, event handlers), and template injection ({{ }}, <% %>, ${})."
      - "Factory function get_default_guard() returns RegexInputGuard. Future ML upgrade: implement MLInputGuard loading a local ONNX classifier, swap in get_default_guard()."
      - "Integration point: input_guard.py module, called from run_command.py before entrypoint execution."
      - "Type-aware checking enables the same guard module to handle both current single-string input and future parameterized inputs (-e, -i, -d, -u) with appropriate pattern subsets per input type."
      - "The guard is a genuine differentiator — no other agent packaging tool provides input-level safety checks."
      - "Strong interview talking point for 'defense in depth' and 'secure-by-default' design patterns."
      - see feature15-notes.md for more code details
    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature3, feature15]
    status: not-started

  - id: feature19
    title: "kinnoo import — Analyzer-backed onboarding wizard"
    description: |
      Add a guided onboarding flow for existing agents: `kinnoo import
      <existing-agent-path> <new-agent-dir>`. The command uses static analysis
      from feature27's analyzer module to infer kinnoo.yaml fields, then runs an
      interactive confirmation wizard. The wizard first presents detected values
      and only asks follow-up questions for fields that could not be inferred.

      The flow creates a Kinnoo-compatible scaffold, writes `kinnoo.yaml` with
      safe defaults and confidence-aware warnings, copies required artifacts for
      run/pack flows, and leaves the source project unchanged.
    tasks: [task141, task142, task143, task144, task145]
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "`kinnoo import <existing-agent-path> <new-agent-dir>` validates arguments and prints clear usage/help when arguments are missing."
      - id: AC2
        description: "Import creates a new Kinnoo agent directory with required files (`kinnoo.yaml`, `requirements.txt`, entrypoint, README, `tools/`, `prompts/`) and does not modify the original source project."
      - id: AC3
        description: "`kinnoo import` invokes feature27 analyzer detectors and generates `kinnoo.yaml` with inferred fields plus confidence-aware warnings when a field cannot be inferred confidently."
      - id: AC4
        description: "Interactive wizard behavior is confirm-first: detected values are shown for user confirmation, and prompts are only shown for missing/ambiguous fields."
      - id: AC5
        description: "If import fails at any step, partial output in `<new-agent-dir>` is cleaned up (or rolled back) so users are not left with a broken half-created agent."
      - id: AC6
        description: "If user interrupts (Ctrl+C/EOF) during interactive confirmation, import exits safely with non-zero status and leaves no partial artifacts."
      - id: AC7
        description: "Collision and safety checks prevent overwrites unless an explicit force/confirm path is used; error messages remain clear and actionable."
      - id: AC8
        description: "Imported agent can be executed via `kinnoo run <new-agent-dir> \"<input>\"` after standard dependency installation path."
      - id: AC9
        description: "For schema fields introduced in features23-26 (for example `runtime.type: mcp-server`, `services`, and MCP permissions), wizard prompts are conditional: ask only when analyzers cannot infer values or when detector confidence is below threshold."
    notes:
      - "Redesign scope: import UX should minimize prompt count; default behavior is accept detected values with one confirmation step."
      - "feature27 analyzers are the single inference backend for import; avoid duplicating heuristics inside import_command."
      - "Import summary should clearly separate: detected values, user-overrides, and unresolved TODO/warnings."
      - "Deferred implementation planning lives in notes/tasks-todo-later.md and notes/tests-todo-later.md while feature23-feature26 are implemented first."
    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature2, feature3, feature9, feature27]
    status: not-started

  - id: feature20
    title: "Flexible Runtime Inputs — No-input run & pass-through arguments"
    description: |
      Extend `kinnoo run` to support agents that require no user input (self-contained
      agents) and agents that accept multiple typed arguments via a `--` pass-through
      separator. Add `inputs.required` (boolean, default true) to the manifest schema
      so agents can declare they need no input. Pass-through arguments after `--` are
      forwarded verbatim to the agent subprocess. The input guard is extended to scan
      each pass-through argument individually.

      Usage patterns:
        kinnoo run myagent                        # no-input (inputs.required: false)
        kinnoo run myagent "hello"                 # current single-input (unchanged)
        kinnoo run myagent -- -e "text" -u "url"  # pass-through mode

      Backward compatibility: the current single positional input mode MUST continue to
      work identically. Only agents with `inputs.required: false` may omit input.
    tasks: [task121, task122, task123, task124, task125]
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "`kinnoo run <dir>` without input succeeds when manifest has `inputs.required: false`; agent receives no positional input argument."
      - id: AC2
        description: "`kinnoo run <dir>` without input fails with a clear error when manifest has `inputs.required: true` (default) or when `inputs.required` is absent."
      - id: AC3
        description: "`kinnoo run <dir> \"hello\"` continues to work identically to V2 behavior (single positional input)."
      - id: AC4
        description: "`kinnoo run <dir> -- -e \"text\" -u \"url\"` forwards all arguments after `--` to the agent subprocess as additional argv entries."
      - id: AC5
        description: "The input guard scans each pass-through argument individually before execution; detected threats are aggregated and displayed."
      - id: AC6
        description: "`--no-guard` flag still disables the guard for all input modes (no-input, single, pass-through)."
      - id: AC7
        description: "Manifest validator accepts `inputs.required` as an optional boolean field; non-boolean values produce a clear type error."
      - id: AC8
        description: "Existing V2 tests for `kinnoo run` continue to pass without modification (regression check required)."
    notes:
      - "REGRESSION RISK: changes argparse for `kinnoo run` — input is currently a required positional arg. SWE agent must run full `test_cli.py` and `test_install.py` regression suite after changes."
      - "Use `argparse.REMAINDER` to capture args after `--` separator."
      - "Preserve backward compat: if no `--` and no input, check `inputs.required` to decide error vs proceed."
      - "Input guard `check_inputs()` multi-value method (from feature18) is the integration point for scanning pass-through args."
    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature3, feature18]
    status: completed

  - id: feature22
    title: "Asset Bundling"
    description: |
      Add a manifest `assets` section for declaring static files and directories to be
      bundled alongside agent code. Declared assets are included in the `.kno` archive
      during `kinnoo pack` and extracted during `kinnoo install` when bundling is enabled.
      Size warnings are displayed when bundled assets push the archive beyond configurable
      thresholds.

      Manifest syntax:
      ```yaml
      assets:
        paths:
          - data/embeddings.npz
          - data/reference_docs/
          - models/classifier.onnx
        bundle: true
        max_bundle_size_mb: 100
      ```

      Use cases: local vector DBs, embedding files, reference documents, model weights.
    tasks: [task135, task136, task137, task138, task139, task140]
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "Manifest validator accepts an optional `assets` field as an object with `paths` (list[string]), optional `bundle` (bool, default true), and optional `max_bundle_size_mb` (number, default 100). Invalid structure produces clear errors."
      - id: AC2
        description: "`kinnoo pack` includes all declared asset paths (files and directories, recursively) in the archive under their original relative paths when `assets.bundle` is true (default)."
      - id: AC3
        description: "`kinnoo pack` skips asset inclusion when `assets.bundle: false` and prints a clear informational message that asset bundling is disabled."
      - id: AC4
        description: "`kinnoo pack` rejects asset paths that use path traversal (e.g., `../secret`) with a clear security error."
      - id: AC5
        description: "`kinnoo pack` warns if a declared asset path does not exist in the agent directory."
      - id: AC6
        description: "`kinnoo install` extracts bundled asset files and directories to their correct relative paths in the installed agent directory."
      - id: AC7
        description: "`kinnoo pack` warns when total archive size exceeds 100 MB by default, or the configured `assets.max_bundle_size_mb` when present."
      - id: AC8
        description: "`kinnoo inspect` displays declared asset paths and their sizes when inspecting an agent or archive."
      - id: AC9
        description: "Agents without an `assets` section are unaffected — pack/install behavior is identical to V2 (regression check required)."
      - id: AC10
        description: "`kinnoo pack` performs a filename-based secret check for asset paths and warns on known credential-like patterns (for example `.env`, `.pem`, `.key`, `id_rsa`, `credentials.json`, `*.p12`, `*.pfx`)."
      - id: AC11
        description: "`kinnoo pack` performs a regex-based credential scan on text asset files (UTF-8, size-limited), warns on likely secret patterns, and skips binary files for this scan."
      - id: AC12
        description: "Asset credential scan findings are non-blocking warnings during pack, with a disclaimer that heuristic scanning may produce false positives and is not a substitute for manual review."
    notes:
      - "REGRESSION RISK: changes pack and install archive handling. SWE agent must run `test_pack.py`, `test_cli_install.py`, and `test_cli_install_extract.py` regression tests."
      - "Use `assets` naming in manifest for clarity and future extensibility; `data/` remains a valid folder name users can reference in `assets.paths`."
      - "Reuse existing `files` inclusion logic where possible but keep `assets` semantically separate for clearer UX."
      - "Enforce deterministic archive paths to avoid install-time path mismatches."
      - "Path traversal check already exists in pack_command.py for extra files — extend it to asset paths."
      - "Asset scanning at pack-time is warning-only for local workflows; consider stricter/blocking checks during publish in a future feature."
    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature5, feature8]
    status: completed

  - id: feature23
    title: "MCP Server Runtime Type — Schema & Lifecycle"
    description: |
      Add `mcp-server` as a supported `runtime.type` in the manifest schema. MCP servers
      are long-running processes (as opposed to one-shot agents). Implement a supervisor
      module that manages the MCP server lifecycle: spawn, readiness probe, signal handling,
      and graceful teardown. When `kinnoo run` is invoked on an agent whose manifest
      declares `runtime.type: mcp-server`, the runtime launches the server process and
      keeps it alive until the user sends SIGINT (Ctrl+C).

      This establishes the foundation for packaging and distributing MCP servers via kinnoo.
    tasks: []
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "Manifest validator accepts `runtime.type: mcp-server` as a valid runtime type alongside `one-shot`."
      - id: AC2
        description: "`kinnoo run` on an `mcp-server` agent spawns the entrypoint as a long-running subprocess (does not wait for it to exit like one-shot)."
      - id: AC3
        description: "The supervisor performs a readiness probe (configurable: TCP port check or stdout marker) before reporting the server as running."
      - id: AC4
        description: "Ctrl+C (SIGINT) triggers graceful shutdown: sends SIGTERM to server, waits for exit (with timeout), then SIGKILL if unresponsive."
      - id: AC5
        description: "Server stdout/stderr are streamed to the terminal in real-time, matching one-shot behavior."
      - id: AC6
        description: "Trace log records server start time, stop time, and exit code/signal."
      - id: AC7
        description: "Existing one-shot agents are completely unaffected by this change (regression check required)."
      - id: AC8
        description: "A manifest with `runtime.type: mcp-server` and no readiness probe configuration falls back to a default TCP check or immediate-ready."
    notes:
      - "REGRESSION RISK: adding `mcp-server` to SUPPORTED_RUNTIME_TYPES in schema.py changes validation behavior. SWE agent must run `test_validator.py` regression tests — existing tests that assert only 'one-shot' is valid will need updating."
      - "Implement lifecycle as a standalone supervisor module (src/kinnoo/supervisor.py) — do NOT embed lifecycle logic inline in run_command.py."
      - "Signal handling should use Python's signal module; test with mock subprocess."
      - "Readiness probe options: TCP port (manifest field `runtime.port`), stdout marker string, or skip (immediate-ready)."
    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature3, feature9]
    status: not-started

  - id: feature24
    title: "Service Declarations — Manifest Schema"
    description: |
      Add an optional `services` section to the kinnoo.yaml manifest schema for declaring
      external service dependencies. Each service entry declares a name, type, and health
      check configuration. The validator ensures correct structure and types. This is a
      schema-only feature — runtime health checks are implemented in feature25.

      Manifest syntax:
      ```yaml
      services:
        - name: my-vector-db
          type: vector-db
          health_check:
            method: tcp
            port: 6333
        - name: my-api
          type: api
          health_check:
            method: http
            url: http://localhost:8000/health
      ```

      Supported service types: mcp-server, vector-db, database, api, local-process.
      Supported health check methods: http, tcp, process.
    tasks: []
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "Manifest validator accepts an optional `services` field as a list of service objects."
      - id: AC2
        description: "Each service object requires `name` (string) and `type` (string from allowed set: mcp-server, vector-db, database, api, local-process). Missing fields produce clear errors."
      - id: AC3
        description: "Each service object accepts an optional `health_check` object with `method` (string from: http, tcp, process) and method-specific fields (`port` for tcp, `url` for http, `process_name` for process)."
      - id: AC4
        description: "Invalid service type or health check method produces a clear error listing the allowed values."
      - id: AC5
        description: "Agents without a `services` section pass validation unchanged (no regression)."
      - id: AC6
        description: "`kinnoo inspect` displays declared services with their names, types, and health check configurations."
      - id: AC7
        description: "Duplicate service names within a single manifest produce a validation error."
    notes:
      - "Schema-only feature — no runtime behavior changes. Health check execution is feature25."
      - "Keep the service type set extensible: validate against a known list but structure for future additions."
      - "SWE agent should add new schema constants (SUPPORTED_SERVICE_TYPES, SUPPORTED_HEALTH_CHECK_METHODS) to schema.py following existing patterns."
    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature9]
    status: not-started

  - id: feature25
    title: "Service Health Checks — Runtime Preflight"
    description: |
      Implement runtime health checks for services declared in the manifest's `services`
      section. Before agent execution, `kinnoo run` performs preflight health checks on
      all declared services. Health check methods: HTTP GET (expects 2xx), TCP port probe,
      process name check (via `pgrep` or equivalent). Results integrate with the existing
      `--preflight` flag output.

      Behavior:
      - Interactive mode: warn on failed checks, prompt user to proceed or abort
      - Non-interactive mode: fail-fast on any failed health check
      - `--preflight` mode: report all service health check results without executing
    tasks: []
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "`kinnoo run` checks health of all declared services before executing the agent. Failed checks display service name, type, and actionable guidance."
      - id: AC2
        description: "HTTP health check performs a GET request to the declared URL and expects a 2xx status code. Timeout is 5 seconds (configurable)."
      - id: AC3
        description: "TCP health check attempts a socket connection to the declared port on localhost. Timeout is 3 seconds (configurable)."
      - id: AC4
        description: "Process health check verifies a process with the declared name is running."
      - id: AC5
        description: "In interactive mode, failed health checks produce a warning and prompt: 'Service <name> is not healthy. Proceed anyway? [y/N]'. In non-interactive mode, failed checks abort execution."
      - id: AC6
        description: "`kinnoo run --preflight` includes service health check results in its output alongside existing preflight checks."
      - id: AC7
        description: "Agents without declared services have no health check behavior — identical to V2 (no regression)."
      - id: AC8
        description: "Health check failures do not hard-block execution in interactive mode — the user can always proceed after the warning."
    notes:
      - "Depends on feature24 for schema; depends on feature14 for --preflight integration."
      - "Use stdlib `socket` for TCP checks, `urllib.request` for HTTP checks to avoid adding dependencies."
      - "Implement health checkers as a small interface (check method → pass/fail + message) in a dedicated module (src/kinnoo/health_check.py)."
    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature24, feature14]
    status: not-started

  - id: feature26
    title: "MCP Server Packages & Client Templates"
    description: |
      Build on the mcp-server runtime type (feature23) to provide:
      1. Packaged MCP server examples — GitHub MCP server and Filesystem MCP server as
         first-party `.kno` archives that can be packed, published, and installed.
      2. Filesystem MCP server permissions — read-only by default, opt-in write+create
         (no delete), `allowed_paths` sandboxing declared in manifest.
      3. MCP client agent templates — new `--framework` options for agents that connect

      The goal is to ship one complete reference pair (MCP server archive + MCP client
      template) as proof-of-concept before expanding the MCP catalog.

      - id: AC3

      - id: AC4

      - id: AC5

      - id: AC6

      - id: AC7

    notes:

      - "REGRESSION RISK: adding `mcp-client` to --framework choices affects init_command.py and cli.py. Run `test_init.py` regression."
      - "Filesystem permissions enforcement should be in the MCP server wrapper code, not in the kinnoo CLI itself."
      - "Start with Filesystem MCP server as the primary reference; GitHub MCP server is secondary."

  - id: feature27
    title: "Project Analyzer Module — Manifest Field Inference"
    description: |
      Add a reusable static analysis module (`src/kinnoo/analyzer.py`) that
      infers kinnoo manifest fields from an existing project directory. The
      analyzer is a detector-based engine used by `kinnoo import` and future
      onboarding workflows to minimize manual `kinnoo.yaml` authoring.

      Initial detectors:
      - `_detect_entrypoint`: infer entrypoint from common files and `__main__`.
      - `_detect_runtime`: infer language/version/type (one-shot vs mcp-server)
        and runtime port hints.
      - `_detect_framework`: infer framework from imports/usages.
      - `_detect_dependencies`: infer dependencies from requirements/pyproject.
      - `_detect_env_vars`: infer env vars from getenv/environ usage.
      - `_detect_assets`: infer bundle candidates from data/model artifacts.
      - `_detect_services`: infer likely external services and health-check hints.

      Analyzer output is structured with inferred values, per-field confidence,
      and warnings so callers can run a confirm-first UX.
    tasks: []
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "A dedicated analyzer module exists (`src/kinnoo/analyzer.py`) with public API `analyze_project(project_dir) -> AnalysisReport` and detector helper functions."
      - id: AC2
        description: "Entrypoint/runtime/framework detection supports common Python agent layouts and emits confidence levels instead of hard failures when uncertain."
      - id: AC3
        description: "Dependency detection reads `requirements.txt` and `pyproject.toml` (project dependencies) and returns normalized package names/constraints."
      - id: AC4
        description: "Environment-variable detection scans source for `os.getenv`, `os.environ[...]`, and equivalent patterns, returning deduplicated env var names."
      - id: AC5
        description: "Asset detection identifies likely bundle candidates (for example `.npz`, `.onnx`, `.bin`, `.db`, model/data directories) with path-safety filtering."
      - id: AC6
        description: "Service detection emits suggested `services` entries based on recognizable connection patterns (for example redis/postgres/http endpoints) with health-check hints where possible."
      - id: AC7
        description: "Analyzer output includes three sections: inferred manifest fields, confidence metadata, and warnings/todo guidance for unresolved fields."
      - id: AC8
        description: "Analyzer is reusable by feature19 import flow without duplicating inference logic in command code."
      - id: AC9
        description: "Analyzer-only tests cover positive detection and uncertain/ambiguous cases for each detector; failures provide actionable diagnostics for debugging detector behavior."
    notes:
      - "Design constraint: detector functions should be independent and composable; each detector returns value + confidence + evidence string."
      - "Prefer stdlib parsing first (regex/ast/pathlib/tomllib); avoid heavyweight optional dependencies in the analyzer core."
      - "This feature is onboarding infrastructure and should be implemented before the full feature19 wizard UX."
      - "Deferred implementation planning lives in notes/tasks-todo-later.md and notes/tests-todo-later.md while feature23-feature26 are implemented first."
    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature20, feature22, feature23, feature24, feature26]
    status: not-started

  - id: feature28
    title: "Registry Backend Abstraction & Remote Client"
    description: |
      Extract the current local mock registry logic behind a formal `RegistryBackend`
      protocol/interface. Implement a `RemoteRegistryClient` that communicates with a
      remote registry server via HTTP. Update CLI commands (`publish`, `install`, `search`,
      `list`) to use the backend abstraction, defaulting to local when no remote is
      configured. Configuration via `~/.kinnoo/config.yaml` or env var
      `KINNOO_REGISTRY_URL`.

      This is the client-side foundation for the remote registry. The server is feature29.
    tasks: []
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "A `RegistryBackend` protocol exists defining methods: `publish(archive_path) -> result`, `resolve(name, version) -> archive_path`, `search(query) -> list`, `list_agents() -> list`."
      - id: AC2
        description: "`LocalRegistryBackend` implements the protocol using existing local mock registry logic — all existing `--local` behavior is preserved."
      - id: AC3
        description: "`RemoteRegistryClient` implements the protocol via HTTP calls to a configurable server URL."
      - id: AC4
        description: "Registry URL is configurable via `~/.kinnoo/config.yaml` (`registry_url` field) or `KINNOO_REGISTRY_URL` env var (env var takes precedence)."
      - id: AC5
        description: "`kinnoo publish` (without `--local`) uses the remote backend when a registry URL is configured; falls back to local when not configured."
      - id: AC6
        description: "`kinnoo install <name>` with `--remote` uses the remote backend to resolve and download the archive."
      - id: AC7
        description: "All existing local registry behavior (publish --local, install --local, list --local, search --local) continues to work identically (regression check required)."
      - id: AC8
        description: "Remote client handles HTTP errors gracefully: connection refused, 401 unauthorized, 404 not found, 500 server error — each produces a clear, actionable CLI message."
    notes:
      - "REGRESSION RISK: refactoring publish/install/list/search command internals. SWE agent must run full `test_cli.py`, `test_cli_install.py`, `test_install.py` regression suite."
      - "Use presigned upload/download URLs so the client does not proxy large .kno files through the API."
      - "RemoteRegistryClient should use `urllib.request` (stdlib) to avoid adding `requests` as a dependency. Consider making `requests` optional."
      - "Token-based auth for remote: store token in `~/.kinnoo/config.yaml` under `registry_token`."
    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature13]
    status: not-started

  - id: feature29
    title: "Remote Registry Server"
    description: |
      Implement a FastAPI-based registry server that stores agent archives in S3 and
      maintains a JSON metadata index. The server provides REST endpoints for the CLI
      client (feature28) to publish, install, search, and list agents. Authentication
      uses token-based auth for CLI and session-based auth for the web UI (feature29).

      Server endpoints:
        POST   /api/publish          — upload archive + metadata
        GET    /api/agents           — list all agents (paginated)
        GET    /api/agents/<name>    — get agent metadata + versions
        GET    /api/agents/<name>/<version>/download — presigned download URL
        GET    /api/search?q=<query> — search agents by name/description
        POST   /api/auth/token       — authenticate, get API token

      Metadata schema: name, version, description, author, checksum, upload_timestamp,
      archive_size_bytes.
    tasks: []
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "A FastAPI server application exists in a dedicated `server/` directory with proper project structure (requirements.txt, entry point)."
      - id: AC2
        description: "POST `/api/publish` accepts archive upload with metadata, stores archive in S3 (or S3-compatible storage), and updates JSON metadata index. Duplicate name+version returns 409 Conflict."
      - id: AC3
        description: "GET `/api/agents` returns paginated list of agents with metadata (name, latest version, description, author, archive size)."
      - id: AC4
        description: "GET `/api/agents/<name>/<version>/download` returns a presigned S3 download URL (archive is not proxied through the server)."
      - id: AC5
        description: "GET `/api/search?q=<query>` filters agents by name and description substring match."
      - id: AC6
        description: "POST `/api/auth/token` authenticates a user and returns an API token. All publish endpoints require valid token in Authorization header."
      - id: AC7
        description: "All endpoints return appropriate HTTP status codes (200, 201, 400, 401, 404, 409, 500) with JSON error bodies."
      - id: AC8
        description: "Server tests use FastAPI TestClient and mock S3 — no real AWS credentials required for testing."
    notes:
      - "This is a NEW server application, separate from the CLI package. Create under `server/` directory at project root."
      - "Use presigned URLs for archive upload/download to avoid proxying large files through the server."
      - "Keep metadata schema small: name, version, description, author, checksum, upload_timestamp, archive_size_bytes."
      - "Add pagination (offset/limit) to list and search endpoints from the start."
      - "S3 backend should be behind an abstraction layer for testing with local filesystem or moto."
      - "Server dependencies (fastapi, uvicorn, boto3) go in server/requirements.txt, NOT in the main kinnoo requirements.txt."
    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature28]
    status: not-started

  - id: feature30
    title: "Registry Web UI"
    description: |
      Add a web-based UI to the remote registry server (feature28) using Jinja2 templates
      served by the same FastAPI application. The web UI provides a browser-based interface
      for discovering, browsing, and downloading agents. Authentication uses session-based
      login (separate from CLI token auth).

      Pages:
        /login             — login form with session cookie auth
        /agents            — paginated agent listing table (name, version, author, size, description)
        /agents/<name>     — agent profile page with version history, metadata, and download link
    tasks: []
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "GET `/login` renders a login form; POST `/login` authenticates and sets a session cookie."
      - id: AC2
        description: "GET `/agents` renders a paginated HTML table of all published agents with name, latest version, author, size, and description."
      - id: AC3
        description: "GET `/agents/<name>` renders an agent profile page showing all versions, metadata, and a download button for each version."
      - id: AC4
        description: "Download button generates a presigned URL and redirects the browser to download the archive directly from S3."
      - id: AC5
        description: "Unauthenticated access to `/agents` and `/agents/<name>` is allowed (read-only browsing). Publishing requires login."
      - id: AC6
        description: "HTML pages are rendered via Jinja2 templates with consistent styling (simple CSS, no JavaScript framework required)."
      - id: AC7
        description: "Web UI tests use FastAPI TestClient to verify page rendering and authentication flows."
    notes:
      - "This feature extends the server from feature28 — same FastAPI app, additional routes and templates."
      - "Keep the UI simple: Jinja2 + plain CSS. No React/Vue/frontend build tools."
      - "Read-only browsing without login is intentional — lowers friction for agent discovery."
      - "Jinja2 templates go in server/templates/."
    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature29]
    status: not-started

# This file contains a list of the tasks implemented by SWE agents - numbered task0, task1, task2, etc.
# Each new task should just increment the task number.
# The current task types are: 
#   - task: any general task to be implemented with code or through command(s)
#   - issue: anything that needs to be resolved - e.g., bug
#   - decision: any decision that needs to be made - e.g., choosing a model
#
# This file contains the project tasks as YAML entries. Use the top-level `tasks` list.
# Each task should reference its parent feature and list any test IDs it owns.
# The validator script `src/validate_project_manifests.py` will enforce unique IDs and references.
#
# Important Note: dependencies field can be other tasks, OR external packages, libraries, frameworks - with the version - that need to be installed in order to complete the task 
#
# Template (YAML):
# tasks:
#   - id: taskX
#     title: Short title
#     type: Task type (defaults to "task" if omitted)
#     description: Short description of the work
#     files: [path/to/file1, path/to/file2]
#     steps:
#       - Step 1 description
#       - Step 2 description
#     dependencies: [taskZ, boto3]
#     tests: [test0, test1]

#
# A decision task has different fields:
#
# Template for decision tasks (YAML):
# tasks:
#   - id: taskX
#     title: Short title
#     type: decision
#     description: Description of the decision to be made. Can include some initial choices, if available.
#     options: Potential choices for the decision (e.g., choice of model), as a YAML style list. Populated once these are available.
#           - option1: overview/pros/cons/artifacts
#           - option2: overview/pros/cons/artifacts
#     criteria: list of measurable evaluation criteria (latency, accuracy, size, license)
#     selected_option: option id (set when status: approved)

#     status: not-started / in-progress / etc

  - id: task116
    title: InputGuard protocol, result models, and factory function
    type: task
    description: |
      Create `src/kinnoo/input_guard.py` with the core architecture for the input safety
      guard system. Define result models (`InputGuardResult`, `InputWarning`), the
      `InputGuard` Protocol with two methods (`check` for single values and `check_inputs`
      for multi-value parameterized input), threat category constants, and the
      `get_default_guard()` factory function. This task establishes the pluggable contract:
      any class satisfying the Protocol can replace the regex guard (e.g., an ML classifier)
      by changing only the factory function.
    files:
      - src/kinnoo/input_guard.py
    steps:
      - 'step1: Create `src/kinnoo/input_guard.py`'
      - 'step2: Define `InputWarning` dataclass with fields: `threat_category: str`, `description: str`, `param_name: str | None = None`'
      - 'step3: Define `InputGuardResult` dataclass with fields: `safe: bool`, `warnings: list[InputWarning]`'
      - 'step4: Define threat category string constants: SQL_INJECTION, SHELL_INJECTION, PATH_TRAVERSAL, SSRF, XSS, TEMPLATE_INJECTION'
      - 'step5: Define `InputGuard` Protocol class with methods: `check(self, value: str, input_type: str = "text") -> InputGuardResult` and `check_inputs(self, inputs: list[tuple[str, str, str]]) -> InputGuardResult` where each tuple is (param_name, value, input_type)'
      - 'step6: Define `get_default_guard() -> InputGuard` factory function that returns `RegexInputGuard()` (placeholder class for now, fully implemented in task117)'
      - 'step7: Ensure the module is importable and `get_default_guard()` returns an instance with both `check` and `check_inputs` methods'
    dependencies: []
    tests: [test149, test150]
    status: completed

  - id: task117
    title: "RegexInputGuard — comprehensive injection pattern library"
    type: task
    description: |
      Implement the full `RegexInputGuard` class in `src/kinnoo/input_guard.py` with
      comprehensive regex patterns for 6 threat categories. Each pattern is a tuple of
      (compiled_regex, threat_category, human_description). The guard supports type-aware
      checking: different input_type values activate different pattern subsets. The
      `check_inputs()` method aggregates results across multiple typed parameters for
      future parameterized input support (-e, -i, -d, -u flags).

      Threat categories and patterns to implement:

      **SQL Injection** (SQL_INJECTION):
      - UNION SELECT / UNION ALL SELECT
      - DROP TABLE / DROP DATABASE
      - INSERT INTO ... VALUES
      - DELETE FROM
      - Tautology: OR 1=1, OR '1'='1', OR ''='', AND 1=1
      - Comment injection: --, #, /* (as SQL comment starters following injection context)
      - WAITFOR DELAY (time-based blind SQLi)
      - EXEC xp_ (stored procedure injection)
      - Stacked queries: semicolon followed by SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DROP

      **Shell Injection** (SHELL_INJECTION):
      - Command chaining: ; & | && || followed by dangerous commands (rm, cat, wget, curl,
        sudo, sh, bash, python, chmod, chown, nc, ncat, mkfifo, dd, kill)
      - Command substitution: $(...) and backtick `...`
      - Pipe to shell: | sh, | bash, | /bin/sh, | /bin/bash
      - Input/output redirection: > /etc/, >> /etc/, < /etc/
      - Null byte injection: \x00, %00

      **Path Traversal** (PATH_TRAVERSAL):
      - ../ and ..\ sequences (2+ levels)
      - URL-encoded variants: %2e%2e%2f, %2e%2e/, ..%2f
      - Double-encoding: %252e%252e%252f
      - Absolute sensitive paths: /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /proc/self, /dev/

      **SSRF** (SSRF):
      - Dangerous protocols: file://, gopher://, dict://, ldap://
      - Internal IPs: 127.0.0.1, 0.0.0.0, 10.x.x.x, 172.16-31.x.x, 192.168.x.x
      - IPv6 loopback: [::1], ::1 (as URL host)
      - localhost as hostname
      - Octal IP: 0177.0.0.1
      - AWS metadata endpoint: 169.254.169.254

      **XSS** (XSS):
      - <script tags (with variations like <ScRiPt, <script/src)
      - javascript: URI scheme
      - Event handlers: onerror=, onload=, onclick=, onmouseover=, onfocus=
      - Dangerous tags with event sources: <img, <iframe, <svg, <object, <embed
      - data:text/html

      **Template Injection** (TEMPLATE_INJECTION):
      - Jinja2/Twig: {{ and }}
      - ERB: <% and %>
      - Expression language: ${...}, #{...}

      **Type-aware input_type filtering:**
      - "text" or "string": all 6 categories
      - "file_path": PATH_TRAVERSAL + SHELL_INJECTION only
      - "url": SSRF + SHELL_INJECTION only
      - "id": SQL_INJECTION + SHELL_INJECTION + TEMPLATE_INJECTION only

      **check_inputs() multi-value aggregation:**
      - Iterate over (param_name, value, input_type) tuples
      - Call check(value, input_type) for each
      - Set param_name on each resulting InputWarning
      - Merge all warnings; safe = True only if all inputs are safe
    files:
      - src/kinnoo/input_guard.py
    steps:
      - 'step1: Define PATTERNS dict mapping threat category -> list of (regex_str, human_description) tuples'
      - 'step2: Define TYPE_FILTER dict mapping input_type -> set of applicable threat categories'
      - 'step3: Implement RegexInputGuard.check(value, input_type) — compile and match patterns filtered by input_type, return InputGuardResult with InputWarning for each match'
      - 'step4: Implement RegexInputGuard.check_inputs(inputs) — iterate over (param_name, value, input_type) tuples, aggregate results, set param_name on warnings'
      - 'step5: Add inline documentation for each pattern explaining what it catches and potential false positives'
      - 'step6: Ensure each pattern can be tested individually via the PATTERNS dict'
    dependencies: [task116]
    tests: [test151, test152, test153, test154, test155, test156, test157, test158, test159]
    status: completed

  - id: task118
    title: "CLI --no-guard flag and run_command integration"
    type: task
    description: |
      Add the `--no-guard` flag to the `kinnoo run` subcommand in cli.py and integrate
      the InputGuard into run_command.py. The guard runs after env var resolution but
      before entrypoint execution. When the guard flags input as unsafe, the user is
      warned and prompted to proceed. Non-interactive stdin (no TTY) auto-aborts as a
      fail-safe to prevent unattended execution of flagged input. The --no-guard flag
      skips the guard entirely for CI/automation pipelines.
    files:
      - src/kinnoo/cli.py
      - src/kinnoo/run_command.py
    steps:

      - 'step2: Pass `no_guard=bool(getattr(args, "no_guard", False))` to `run_agent()` call in cli.py'
      - 'step3: Add `no_guard: bool = False` parameter to `run_agent()` signature in run_command.py'
      - 'step4: In run_command.py, after env var resolution and before entrypoint execution, add guard integration block:
        - If not no_guard and input_arg is not None:
          - Import get_default_guard from input_guard
          - Call guard.check(input_arg, "text")
          - If not result.safe:
            - Print "[kinnoo] Input safety warning:" to stderr
            - For each warning, print "  - [{threat_category}] {description}" to stderr
            - If sys.stdin.isatty(): prompt "Proceed anyway? [y/N]: " and read response
            - If not sys.stdin.isatty() (non-interactive): print "Non-interactive mode: aborting." to stderr and return finalize(1)
            - If response is not "y" (case-insensitive): return finalize(1)
            - Handle KeyboardInterrupt and EOFError during prompt gracefully (abort with exit 1)'
      - 'step5: Ensure --no-guard bypasses the entire guard block (no import, no check, no prompt)'
      - 'step6: Ensure the guard does not run in preflight mode (preflight=True already returns early, but verify)'

```plaintext
# This file contains a list of the test cases written by SWE agents - numbered test0, test1, etc.
# Each new test case should just increment the test number.
#
# Template (YAML):
# tests:
#   - id: testX
#     title: One-line title
#     type: unit|integration|e2e|manual
#     preconditions: e.g., iPhone 12, iOS 15, camera permission granted
#     steps:
#       - Step 1
#       - Step 2
#     expected: Short expected result
#     pass_criteria: Measurable pass criteria
#     automated: true|false
#     automation_path: path/to/test (if automated)
#
# Example:
# tests:
#   - id: test0
#     title: Capture action stores image in buffer
#     type: integration
#     preconditions: App running on iPhone 12 (iOS 15), camera permission granted
#     steps:
#       - step1: Open the camera view
#       - step2: Tap the white capture button
#     expected: An image is captured and stored in the temporary buffer
#     pass_criteria: buffer non-empty and capture recorded within 200ms of tap
#     automated: false
#     automation_path: null
#
#   - id: test1
#     title: Capture button visible bottom-center
#     type: e2e
#     preconditions: App running on iPhone 12 (iOS 15)
#     steps:
#       - step1: Open camera view in portrait
#       - step2: Observe UI layout
#     expected: White capture button is visible bottom-center across supported devices
#     pass_criteria: visible on iPhone12/13/14 portrait
#     automated: false
#     automation_path: null

tests:
  - id: test0
    title: Valid manifest passes validation
    type: unit
    preconditions: validator module available, PyYAML installed
    steps:
      - step1: Create a kinnoo.yaml with all required fields and valid values
      - step2: Call validate(path)
    expected: Returns (True, [])
    pass_criteria: is_valid is True and errors list is empty
    covers:
      - feature: feature1
        ac: AC1
    automated: true
    automation_path: tests/test_validator.py::test_valid_manifest_passes

  - id: test1
    title: Missing required field produces specific error

      - step2: Call validate(path)
    expected: Returns (False, [...]) with error message naming 'entrypoint'
    pass_criteria: is_valid is False; errors list contains a string mentioning 'entrypoint'
    covers:

        ac: AC2

    automation_path: tests/test_validator.py::test_missing_required_field

  - id: test2

# A feature can be broken down into one or more individual tasks. Each task can be completed by the same SWE agent, or SWE sub-agents if needed.

#
# This file contains the project features as YAML entries. Each feature should
# be represented as an item in the top-level `features` list. Use the template

# Template (YAML):
# features:

features:
  - id: feature1
    title: Manifest schema and validation
    description: |
      Define the kinnoo.yaml manifest schema and implement a validator that parses
      and validates manifest files against it. The validator returns clear, actionable
      error messages and is usable as a library function for other commands (pack, run, etc.).

      Schema definition:
      | Field              | Required | Type         | Constraints                                      |
      |--------------------|----------|--------------|--------------------------------------------------|
      | name               | yes      | string       | non-empty, valid package name (alphanumeric, -)  |
      | version            | yes      | string       | valid semver (e.g., "0.1.0", "1.2.3")            |
      | entrypoint         | yes      | string       | non-empty file path                              |
      | runtime.language   | yes      | string       | e.g., "python"                                   |
      | runtime.version    | yes      | string       | version constraint (e.g., ">=3.10")              |
      | runtime.type       | yes      | string       | e.g., "one-shot"                                 |
      | dependencies       | yes      | list[string] | can be empty list                                |
      | inputs.type        | yes      | string       | e.g., "text"                                     |
      | outputs.type       | yes      | string       | e.g., "text"                                     |
      | framework          | no       | string       | optional, e.g., "langchain"                      |
    tasks: [task0, task1, task2, task3]
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: A kinnoo.yaml with all required fields and valid values passes validation without errors.

    description: |

      current environment -> .env file in agent directory -> interactive masked prompt.

      - id: AC3

      - id: AC4
        description: "All resolved env vars are injected into the subprocess environment when executing the agent."

  - id: feature15
    title: "Trust Baseline"
    description: |
      Add transparency and trust features: display dependency/secret name summary on install,
      warn when installing agents from unverified sources, log run traces, and perform a
      heuristic code sweep for env var value exposure. Absolute rule: no env var or secret
      VALUES ever appear in output, logs, or code paths — only names.
    tasks: [task98, task99, task100, task101, task102, task103, task104]
    acceptance_criteria:

        description: "`kinnoo install` displays a summary of what the agent requires (env_var NAMES, dependency NAMES, runtime type) before installing and prompts for yes/no confirmation. A `--yes` (`-y`) flag skips the confirmation prompt for CI/automation pipelines."
      - id: AC2
        description: "If an agent is installed from a raw .kno file (not from a registry or archive) without an accompanying checksum .kno.sha256 file, a confirmation prompt is asked before proceeding: 'This agent is from an unverified source. Continue? (y/n)'."
      - id: AC3
        description: "`kinnoo run` logs a trace in JSON format to ~/.kinnoo/logs/run.<TIMESTAMP>.log containing ONLY: timestamp, agent name, agent version, runtime type, and exit code — no input content, no env var values, no secrets."
      - id: AC4

      - id: AC5
        description: "All trust-related display and logging code includes inline comments documenting the 'no secret values' invariant."
      - id: AC6
        description: "`kinnoo inspect` includes a heuristic security sweep of all .py files in the agent directory (excluding .venv/) that detects patterns where env var values may be printed, logged, or written to files. Warnings are displayed with file path and line number. A clean scan prints 'Security sweep: no env var exposure patterns detected (heuristic)'. The sweep also runs during `kinnoo pack` as a non-blocking warning before archiving."
    notes:
      - "Original AC4 (first-run display of env/dep names) was dropped — redundant with kinnoo inspect and kinnoo run --preflight."
      - "AC6 is a regex-based heuristic, not taint analysis. Output includes a disclaimer about false positives."

    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature10]
    status: completed

  - id: feature18
    title: "Input Safety Guard"
    description: |
      Add a pluggable input safety check to `kinnoo run` that inspects user-provided input
      for common injection patterns (SQL injection, shell command injection, path traversal,
      SSRF, XSS, template injection) before passing it to the agent entrypoint. The guard is
      non-blocking — it warns and prompts for confirmation rather than hard-rejecting input.
      The architecture uses a Protocol-based design so the V1 regex guard can be swapped for
      an ML-based classifier in the future without changing callers.

      The guard is designed to work with both the current single-string input model
      (`kinnoo run <path> "<input>"`) and a future parameterized input model
      (`kinnoo run <path> -e <string> -i <id> -d <file-path> -u <url>`). For parameterized
      inputs, the guard applies type-aware pattern filtering: file path inputs emphasize path
      traversal detection, URL inputs emphasize SSRF detection, ID inputs enforce stricter
      injection patterns. A `check_inputs()` multi-value method accepts typed parameters so
      callers can pass all inputs in a single call and receive an aggregated result.
    tasks: [task116, task117, task118, task119, task120]
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "`kinnoo run` checks user input against injection patterns (SQL injection, shell command injection, path traversal, SSRF, XSS, template injection) before executing the agent entrypoint."
      - id: AC2
        description: "When a pattern match is found, a warning is printed to stderr listing the detected threat(s), and the user is prompted with 'Proceed anyway? [y/N]'. Answering 'n' or empty aborts with non-zero exit. Answering 'y' proceeds normally. Non-interactive stdin (no TTY) auto-aborts as a fail-safe."
      - id: AC3
        description: "A `--no-guard` flag on `kinnoo run` disables the input safety check entirely for CI/automation pipelines where input is controlled."
      - id: AC4
        description: "The guard implementation follows a Protocol-based pluggable design (`InputGuard` protocol with `check(value, input_type) -> InputGuardResult` and `check_inputs(inputs) -> InputGuardResult`) so the regex-based guard can be replaced with an ML-based guard via a single factory function change."
      - id: AC5
        description: "Each regex pattern in the V1 guard is individually unit-testable and documented with the threat category it detects."
      - id: AC6
        description: "Legitimate agent input that happens to resemble injection (e.g., a database agent receiving SQL) is not hard-blocked — the user can always proceed after the warning."
      - id: AC7
        description: "The guard supports type-aware input checking: 'text' (full scan), 'file_path' (path traversal + shell injection), 'url' (SSRF + shell injection), 'id' (SQL + shell + template injection), enabling future parameterized input modes (-e, -i, -d, -u) without code changes."
      - id: AC8
        description: "A `check_inputs()` method accepts a list of (param_name, value, input_type) tuples and returns an aggregated result with per-parameter warnings, ready for future multi-parameter input."
    notes:
      - "V1 uses RegexInputGuard with patterns for 6 threat categories: SQL injection (UNION SELECT, DROP TABLE, tautology, comment injection, WAITFOR DELAY), shell injection (;&| with dangerous commands, $() and backtick substitution, pipe to shell), path traversal (../, encoded variants, absolute sensitive paths), SSRF (file://, gopher://, dict://, internal IPs, AWS metadata 169.254.169.254), XSS (<script, javascript:, event handlers), and template injection ({{ }}, <% %>, ${})."
      - "Factory function get_default_guard() returns RegexInputGuard. Future ML upgrade: implement MLInputGuard loading a local ONNX classifier, swap in get_default_guard()."
      - "Integration point: input_guard.py module, called from run_command.py before entrypoint execution."
      - "Type-aware checking enables the same guard module to handle both current single-string input and future parameterized inputs (-e, -i, -d, -u) with appropriate pattern subsets per input type."
      - "The guard is a genuine differentiator — no other agent packaging tool provides input-level safety checks."
      - "Strong interview talking point for 'defense in depth' and 'secure-by-default' design patterns."
      - see feature15-notes.md for more code details
    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature3, feature15]
    status: not-started

  - id: feature19
    title: "kinnoo import — Analyzer-backed onboarding wizard"
    description: |
      Add a guided onboarding flow for existing agents: `kinnoo import
      <existing-agent-path> <new-agent-dir>`. The command uses static analysis
      from feature27's analyzer module to infer kinnoo.yaml fields, then runs an
      interactive confirmation wizard. The wizard first presents detected values
      and only asks follow-up questions for fields that could not be inferred.

      The flow creates a Kinnoo-compatible scaffold, writes `kinnoo.yaml` with
      safe defaults and confidence-aware warnings, copies required artifacts for
      run/pack flows, and leaves the source project unchanged.
    tasks: []
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "`kinnoo import <existing-agent-path> <new-agent-dir>` validates arguments and prints clear usage/help when arguments are missing."
      - id: AC2
        description: "Import creates a new Kinnoo agent directory with required files (`kinnoo.yaml`, `requirements.txt`, entrypoint, README, `tools/`, `prompts/`) and does not modify the original source project."
      - id: AC3
        description: "`kinnoo import` invokes feature27 analyzer detectors and generates `kinnoo.yaml` with inferred fields plus confidence-aware warnings when a field cannot be inferred confidently."
      - id: AC4
        description: "Interactive wizard behavior is confirm-first: detected values are shown for user confirmation, and prompts are only shown for missing/ambiguous fields."
      - id: AC5
        description: "If import fails at any step, partial output in `<new-agent-dir>` is cleaned up (or rolled back) so users are not left with a broken half-created agent."
      - id: AC6
        description: "If user interrupts (Ctrl+C/EOF) during interactive confirmation, import exits safely with non-zero status and leaves no partial artifacts."
      - id: AC7
        description: "Collision and safety checks prevent overwrites unless an explicit force/confirm path is used; error messages remain clear and actionable."
      - id: AC8
        description: "Imported agent can be executed via `kinnoo run <new-agent-dir> \"<input>\"` after standard dependency installation path."
      - id: AC9
        description: "For schema fields introduced in features23-26 (for example `runtime.type: mcp-server`, `services`, and MCP permissions), wizard prompts are conditional: ask only when analyzers cannot infer values or when detector confidence is below threshold."
    notes:
      - "Redesign scope: import UX should minimize prompt count; default behavior is accept detected values with one confirmation step."
      - "feature27 analyzers are the single inference backend for import; avoid duplicating heuristics inside import_command."
      - "Import summary should clearly separate: detected values, user-overrides, and unresolved TODO/warnings."
      - "Deferred implementation planning lives in notes/tasks-todo-later.md and notes/tests-todo-later.md while feature23-feature26 are implemented first."
    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature2, feature3, feature9, feature27]
    status: not-started

  - id: feature20
    title: "Flexible Runtime Inputs — No-input run & pass-through arguments"
    description: |
      Extend `kinnoo run` to support agents that require no user input (self-contained
      agents) and agents that accept multiple typed arguments via a `--` pass-through
      separator. Add `inputs.required` (boolean, default true) to the manifest schema
      so agents can declare they need no input. Pass-through arguments after `--` are
      forwarded verbatim to the agent subprocess. The input guard is extended to scan
      each pass-through argument individually.

      Usage patterns:
        kinnoo run myagent                        # no-input (inputs.required: false)
        kinnoo run myagent "hello"                 # current single-input (unchanged)
        kinnoo run myagent -- -e "text" -u "url"  # pass-through mode

      Backward compatibility: the current single positional input mode MUST continue to
      work identically. Only agents with `inputs.required: false` may omit input.
    tasks: [task121, task122, task123, task124, task125]
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "`kinnoo run <dir>` without input succeeds when manifest has `inputs.required: false`; agent receives no positional input argument."
      - id: AC2
        description: "`kinnoo run <dir>` without input fails with a clear error when manifest has `inputs.required: true` (default) or when `inputs.required` is absent."
      - id: AC3
        description: "`kinnoo run <dir> \"hello\"` continues to work identically to V2 behavior (single positional input)."
      - id: AC4
        description: "`kinnoo run <dir> -- -e \"text\" -u \"url\"` forwards all arguments after `--` to the agent subprocess as additional argv entries."
      - id: AC5
        description: "The input guard scans each pass-through argument individually before execution; detected threats are aggregated and displayed."
      - id: AC6
        description: "`--no-guard` flag still disables the guard for all input modes (no-input, single, pass-through)."
      - id: AC7
        description: "Manifest validator accepts `inputs.required` as an optional boolean field; non-boolean values produce a clear type error."
      - id: AC8
        description: "Existing V2 tests for `kinnoo run` continue to pass without modification (regression check required)."
    notes:
      - "REGRESSION RISK: changes argparse for `kinnoo run` — input is currently a required positional arg. SWE agent must run full `test_cli.py` and `test_install.py` regression suite after changes."
      - "Use `argparse.REMAINDER` to capture args after `--` separator."
      - "Preserve backward compat: if no `--` and no input, check `inputs.required` to decide error vs proceed."
      - "Input guard `check_inputs()` multi-value method (from feature18) is the integration point for scanning pass-through args."
    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature3, feature18]
    status: completed
