  - id: feature18
    title: "Input Safety Guard"
    description: |
      Add a pluggable input safety check to `kinnoo run` that inspects user-provided input
      for common injection patterns (SQL injection, shell command injection, path traversal,
      SSRF, XSS, template injection) before passing it to the agent entrypoint. The guard is
      non-blocking — it warns and prompts for confirmation rather than hard-rejecting input.
      The architecture uses a Protocol-based design so the V1 regex guard can be swapped for
      an ML-based classifier in the future without changing callers.

      The guard is designed to work with both the current single-string input model
      (`kinnoo run <path> "<input>"`) and a future parameterized input model
      (`kinnoo run <path> -e <string> -i <id> -d <file-path> -u <url>`). For parameterized
      inputs, the guard applies type-aware pattern filtering: file path inputs emphasize path
      traversal detection, URL inputs emphasize SSRF detection, ID inputs enforce stricter
      injection patterns. A `check_inputs()` multi-value method accepts typed parameters so
      callers can pass all inputs in a single call and receive an aggregated result.
    tasks: [task116, task117, task118, task119, task120]
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "`kinnoo run` checks user input against injection patterns (SQL injection, shell command injection, path traversal, SSRF, XSS, template injection) before executing the agent entrypoint."
      - id: AC2
        description: "When a pattern match is found, a warning is printed to stderr listing the detected threat(s), and the user is prompted with 'Proceed anyway? [y/N]'. Answering 'n' or empty aborts with non-zero exit. Answering 'y' proceeds normally. Non-interactive stdin (no TTY) auto-aborts as a fail-safe."
      - id: AC3
        description: "A `--no-guard` flag on `kinnoo run` disables the input safety check entirely for CI/automation pipelines where input is controlled."
      - id: AC4
        description: "The guard implementation follows a Protocol-based pluggable design (`InputGuard` protocol with `check(value, input_type) -> InputGuardResult` and `check_inputs(inputs) -> InputGuardResult`) so the regex-based guard can be replaced with an ML-based guard via a single factory function change."
      - id: AC5
        description: "Each regex pattern in the V1 guard is individually unit-testable and documented with the threat category it detects."
      - id: AC6
        description: "Legitimate agent input that happens to resemble injection (e.g., a database agent receiving SQL) is not hard-blocked — the user can always proceed after the warning."
      - id: AC7
        description: "The guard supports type-aware input checking: 'text' (full scan), 'file_path' (path traversal + shell injection), 'url' (SSRF + shell injection), 'id' (SQL + shell + template injection), enabling future parameterized input modes (-e, -i, -d, -u) without code changes."
      - id: AC8
        description: "A `check_inputs()` method accepts a list of (param_name, value, input_type) tuples and returns an aggregated result with per-parameter warnings, ready for future multi-parameter input."
    notes:
      - "V1 uses RegexInputGuard with patterns for 6 threat categories: SQL injection (UNION SELECT, DROP TABLE, tautology, comment injection, WAITFOR DELAY), shell injection (;&| with dangerous commands, $() and backtick substitution, pipe to shell), path traversal (../, encoded variants, absolute sensitive paths), SSRF (file://, gopher://, dict://, internal IPs, AWS metadata 169.254.169.254), XSS (<script, javascript:, event handlers), and template injection ({{ }}, <% %>, ${})."
      - "Factory function get_default_guard() returns RegexInputGuard. Future ML upgrade: implement MLInputGuard loading a local ONNX classifier, swap in get_default_guard()."
      - "Integration point: input_guard.py module, called from run_command.py before entrypoint execution."
      - "Type-aware checking enables the same guard module to handle both current single-string input and future parameterized inputs (-e, -i, -d, -u) with appropriate pattern subsets per input type."
      - "The guard is a genuine differentiator — no other agent packaging tool provides input-level safety checks."
      - "Strong interview talking point for 'defense in depth' and 'secure-by-default' design patterns."
      - see feature15-notes.md for more code details
    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature3, feature15]
    status: not-started

  - id: feature19
    title: "kinnoo import — Analyzer-backed onboarding wizard"
    description: |
      Add a guided onboarding flow for existing agents: `kinnoo import [path]`
      (default `.`). The command uses static analysis from feature27's analyzer
      module to infer kinnoo.yaml fields, then runs an interactive confirmation
      wizard. The wizard first presents detected values and only asks follow-up
      questions for fields that could not be inferred.

      The flow writes `kinnoo.yaml` in-place with safe defaults and
      confidence-aware warnings, keeps the source project layout unchanged, and
      avoids file copying/scaffold cloning. Entrypoint compatibility gaps are
      warning-first and non-blocking, with an optional wrapper generation path.
    tasks: [task163, task164, task165, task166, task167]
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "`kinnoo import [path]` validates arguments, defaults to current directory when omitted, and prints clear usage/help when arguments are invalid."
      - id: AC2
        description: "Import writes `kinnoo.yaml` in the target project directory without copying project files or creating a duplicate Kinnoo scaffold; existing source files are not modified."
      - id: AC3
        description: "`kinnoo import` invokes feature27 analyzer detectors and generates `kinnoo.yaml` with inferred fields plus confidence-aware warnings when a field cannot be inferred confidently."
      - id: AC4
        description: "Interactive wizard behavior is confirm-first: detected values are shown for user confirmation, and prompts are only shown for missing/ambiguous fields."
      - id: AC5
        description: "If import fails at any step, partial output in the target project (for example partially written `kinnoo.yaml` or wrapper artifacts) is cleaned up (or rolled back) so users are not left with a broken half-created setup."
      - id: AC6
        description: "If user interrupts (Ctrl+C/EOF) during interactive confirmation, import exits safely with non-zero status and leaves no partial artifacts."
      - id: AC7
        description: "Collision and safety checks prevent overwrites unless an explicit force/confirm path is used; error messages remain clear and actionable."
      - id: AC8
        description: "Imported agent can be executed in-place via `kinnoo run <path> \"<input>\"` (or `kinnoo run . \"<input>\"`) after standard dependency installation path."
      - id: AC9
        description: "For schema fields introduced in features23-26 (for example `runtime.type: mcp-server`, `services`, and MCP permissions), wizard prompts are conditional: ask only when analyzers cannot infer values or when detector confidence is below threshold."
      - id: AC10
        description: "If entrypoint analysis indicates kinnoo input/output contract mismatch, import emits a clear non-blocking warning and offers an optional wrapper generation path instead of failing by default."
    notes:
      - "Redesign scope: import UX should minimize prompt count; default behavior is accept detected values with one confirmation step."
      - "feature27 analyzers are the single inference backend for import; avoid duplicating heuristics inside import_command."
      - "Import summary should clearly separate: detected values, user-overrides, and unresolved TODO/warnings."
      - "Primary UX model is in-place onboarding (metadata layer), not project copying."
      - "Optional wrapper generation is opt-in and only for entrypoint compatibility gaps."
      - "Deferred implementation planning lives in notes/tasks-todo-later.md and notes/tests-todo-later.md while feature23-feature26 are implemented first."
    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature2, feature3, feature9, feature27]
    status: not-started

  # ======================================================================
  # Phase 3 (V3): "Share any agent. Run it with its full stack."
  # ======================================================================

  - id: feature20
    title: "Flexible Runtime Inputs — No-input run & pass-through arguments"
    description: |
      Extend `kinnoo run` to support agents that require no user input (self-contained
      agents) and agents that accept multiple typed arguments via a `--` pass-through
      separator. Add `inputs.required` (boolean, default true) to the manifest schema
      so agents can declare they need no input. Pass-through arguments after `--` are
      forwarded verbatim to the agent subprocess. The input guard is extended to scan
      each pass-through argument individually.

      Usage patterns:
        kinnoo run myagent                        # no-input (inputs.required: false)
        kinnoo run myagent "hello"                 # current single-input (unchanged)
        kinnoo run myagent -- -e "text" -u "url"  # pass-through mode

      Backward compatibility: the current single positional input mode MUST continue to
      work identically. Only agents with `inputs.required: false` may omit input.
    tasks: [task121, task122, task123, task124, task125]
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "`kinnoo run <dir>` without input succeeds when manifest has `inputs.required: false`; agent receives no positional input argument."
      - id: AC2
        description: "`kinnoo run <dir>` without input fails with a clear error when manifest has `inputs.required: true` (default) or when `inputs.required` is absent."
      - id: AC3
        description: "`kinnoo run <dir> \"hello\"` continues to work identically to V2 behavior (single positional input)."
      - id: AC4
        description: "`kinnoo run <dir> -- -e \"text\" -u \"url\"` forwards all arguments after `--` to the agent subprocess as additional argv entries."
      - id: AC5
        description: "The input guard scans each pass-through argument individually before execution; detected threats are aggregated and displayed."
      - id: AC6
        description: "`--no-guard` flag still disables the guard for all input modes (no-input, single, pass-through)."
      - id: AC7
        description: "Manifest validator accepts `inputs.required` as an optional boolean field; non-boolean values produce a clear type error."
      - id: AC8
        description: "Existing V2 tests for `kinnoo run` continue to pass without modification (regression check required)."
    notes:
      - "REGRESSION RISK: changes argparse for `kinnoo run` — input is currently a required positional arg. SWE agent must run full `test_cli.py` and `test_install.py` regression suite after changes."
      - "Use `argparse.REMAINDER` to capture args after `--` separator."
      - "Preserve backward compat: if no `--` and no input, check `inputs.required` to decide error vs proceed."
      - "Input guard `check_inputs()` multi-value method (from feature18) is the integration point for scanning pass-through args."
    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature3, feature18]
    status: completed

  - id: feature21
    title: "Framework & Template Expansion — PydanticAI, LangGraph, OpenAI Agents"
    description: |
      Expand `kinnoo init --framework` to support three new framework templates:
      `pydantic-ai`, `langgraph`, and `openai-agents`. Each template produces a
      minimal but runnable agent scaffold with framework-specific `run.py`, 
      `requirements.txt`, `kinnoo.yaml`, and `README.md`. All templates follow
      a common contract (accept input via sys.argv[1], print output to stdout,
      env vars for API keys) so the kinnoo run/pack/install flow works unchanged.
    tasks: [task126, task127, task128, task129, task130, task131, task132, task133, task134]
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "`kinnoo init my-agent --framework pydantic-ai` creates a directory with PydanticAI agent scaffold including typed tools and multi-model support boilerplate."
      - id: AC2
        description: "`kinnoo init my-agent --framework langgraph` creates a directory with LangGraph stateful graph agent scaffold including nodes and edges boilerplate."
      - id: AC3

  - id: feature22
    title: "Asset Bundling"
    description: |
      Add a manifest `assets` section for declaring static files and directories to be
      bundled alongside agent code. Declared assets are included in the `.kno` archive
      during `kinnoo pack` and extracted during `kinnoo install` when bundling is enabled.
      Size warnings are displayed when bundled assets push the archive beyond configurable
      thresholds.

      Manifest syntax:
      ```yaml
      assets:
        paths:
          - data/embeddings.npz
          - data/reference_docs/
          - models/classifier.onnx
        bundle: true
        max_bundle_size_mb: 100
      ```

      Use cases: local vector DBs, embedding files, reference documents, model weights.
    tasks: [task135, task136, task137, task138, task139, task140]
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "Manifest validator accepts an optional `assets` field as an object with `paths` (list[string]), optional `bundle` (bool, default true), and optional `max_bundle_size_mb` (number, default 100). Invalid structure produces clear errors."
      - id: AC2
        description: "`kinnoo pack` includes all declared asset paths (files and directories, recursively) in the archive under their original relative paths when `assets.bundle` is true (default)."
      - id: AC3
        description: "`kinnoo pack` skips asset inclusion when `assets.bundle: false` and prints a clear informational message that asset bundling is disabled."
      - id: AC4
        description: "`kinnoo pack` rejects asset paths that use path traversal (e.g., `../secret`) with a clear security error."
      - id: AC5
        description: "`kinnoo pack` warns if a declared asset path does not exist in the agent directory."
      - id: AC6
        description: "`kinnoo install` extracts bundled asset files and directories to their correct relative paths in the installed agent directory."
      - id: AC7
        description: "`kinnoo pack` warns when total archive size exceeds 100 MB by default, or the configured `assets.max_bundle_size_mb` when present."
      - id: AC8
        description: "`kinnoo inspect` displays declared asset paths and their sizes when inspecting an agent or archive."
      - id: AC9
        description: "Agents without an `assets` section are unaffected — pack/install behavior is identical to V2 (regression check required)."
      - id: AC10
        description: "`kinnoo pack` performs a filename-based secret check for asset paths and warns on known credential-like patterns (for example `.env`, `.pem`, `.key`, `id_rsa`, `credentials.json`, `*.p12`, `*.pfx`)."
      - id: AC11
        description: "`kinnoo pack` performs a regex-based credential scan on text asset files (UTF-8, size-limited), warns on likely secret patterns, and skips binary files for this scan."
      - id: AC12
        description: "Asset credential scan findings are non-blocking warnings during pack, with a disclaimer that heuristic scanning may produce false positives and is not a substitute for manual review."
    notes:
      - "REGRESSION RISK: changes pack and install archive handling. SWE agent must run `test_pack.py`, `test_cli_install.py`, and `test_cli_install_extract.py` regression tests."
      - "Use `assets` naming in manifest for clarity and future extensibility; `data/` remains a valid folder name users can reference in `assets.paths`."
      - "Reuse existing `files` inclusion logic where possible but keep `assets` semantically separate for clearer UX."
      - "Enforce deterministic archive paths to avoid install-time path mismatches."
      - "Path traversal check already exists in pack_command.py for extra files — extend it to asset paths."
      - "Asset scanning at pack-time is warning-only for local workflows; consider stricter/blocking checks during publish in a future feature."
    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature5, feature8]
    status: completed

  - id: feature23
    title: "MCP Server Runtime Type — Schema & Lifecycle"
    description: |
      Add `mcp-server` as a supported `runtime.type` in the manifest schema. MCP servers
      are long-running processes (as opposed to one-shot agents). Implement a supervisor
      module that manages the MCP server lifecycle: spawn, readiness probe, signal handling,
      and graceful teardown. When `kinnoo run` is invoked on an agent whose manifest
      declares `runtime.type: mcp-server`, the runtime launches the server process and
      keeps it alive until the user sends SIGINT (Ctrl+C).

      This establishes the foundation for packaging and distributing MCP servers via kinnoo.
    tasks: [task141, task142, task143, task144, task145]
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "Manifest validator accepts `runtime.type: mcp-server` as a valid runtime type alongside `one-shot`."
      - id: AC2
        description: "`kinnoo run` on an `mcp-server` agent spawns the entrypoint as a long-running subprocess (does not wait for it to exit like one-shot)."
      - id: AC3
        description: "The supervisor performs a readiness probe (configurable: TCP port check or stdout marker) before reporting the server as running."
      - id: AC4
        description: "Ctrl+C (SIGINT) triggers graceful shutdown: sends SIGTERM to server, waits for exit (with timeout), then SIGKILL if unresponsive."
      - id: AC5
        description: "Server stdout/stderr are streamed to the terminal in real-time, matching one-shot behavior."
      - id: AC6
        description: "Trace log records server start time, stop time, and exit code/signal."
      - id: AC7
        description: "Existing one-shot agents are completely unaffected by this change (regression check required)."
      - id: AC8
        description: "A manifest with `runtime.type: mcp-server` and no readiness probe configuration falls back to a default TCP check or immediate-ready."
    notes:
      - "REGRESSION RISK: adding `mcp-server` to SUPPORTED_RUNTIME_TYPES in schema.py changes validation behavior. SWE agent must run `test_validator.py` regression tests — existing tests that assert only 'one-shot' is valid will need updating."
      - "Implement lifecycle as a standalone supervisor module (src/kinnoo/supervisor.py) — do NOT embed lifecycle logic inline in run_command.py."
      - "Signal handling should use Python's signal module; test with mock subprocess."
      - "Readiness probe options: TCP port (manifest field `runtime.port`), stdout marker string, or skip (immediate-ready)."
    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature3, feature9]
    status: completed

  - id: feature24
    title: "Service Declarations — Manifest Schema"
    description: |
      Add an optional `services` section to the kinnoo.yaml manifest schema for declaring
      external service dependencies. Each service entry declares a name, type, and health
      check configuration. The validator ensures correct structure and types. This is a
      schema-only feature — runtime health checks are implemented in feature25.

      Manifest syntax:
      ```yaml
      services:
        - name: my-vector-db
          type: vector-db
          health_check:
            method: tcp
            port: 6333
        - name: my-api
          type: api
          health_check:
            method: http
            url: http://localhost:8000/health
      ```

      Supported service types: mcp-server, vector-db, database, api, local-process.
      Compatibility aliases accepted: postgres, redis, http-api, process.
      Supported health check methods: http, tcp, process.
    tasks: [task146, task147, task148, task149]
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "Manifest validator accepts an optional `services` field as a list of service objects."
      - id: AC2
        description: "Each service object requires `name` (string) and `type` (string from allowed set: mcp-server, vector-db, database, api, local-process; compatibility aliases: postgres, redis, http-api, process). Missing fields produce clear errors."
      - id: AC3
        description: "Each service object accepts an optional `health_check` object; when `health_check` is present, `method` is required (string from: http, tcp, process) and method-specific fields apply (`port` for tcp, `url` for http, `process_name` for process)."
      - id: AC4
        description: "Invalid service type or health check method produces a clear error listing the allowed values."
      - id: AC5
        description: "Agents without a `services` section pass validation unchanged (no regression)."
      - id: AC6
        description: "`kinnoo inspect` displays declared services with their names, types, and health check configurations."
      - id: AC7
        description: "Duplicate service names within a single manifest produce a validation error."
    notes:
      - "Schema-only feature — no runtime behavior changes. Health check execution is feature25."
      - "Keep the service type set extensible: validate against a known list but structure for future additions."
      - "SWE agent should add new schema constants (SUPPORTED_SERVICE_TYPES, SUPPORTED_HEALTH_CHECK_METHODS) to schema.py following existing patterns."
    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature9]
    status: completed

  - id: feature25
    title: "Service Health Checks — Runtime Preflight"
    description: |
      Implement runtime health checks for services declared in the manifest's `services`
      section. Before agent execution, `kinnoo run` performs preflight health checks on
      all declared services. Health check methods: HTTP GET (expects 2xx), TCP port probe,
      process name check (via `pgrep` or equivalent). Results integrate with the existing
      `--preflight` flag output.

      Behavior:
      - Interactive mode: warn on failed checks, prompt user to proceed or abort
      - Non-interactive mode: fail-fast on any failed health check
      - `--preflight` mode: report all service health check results without executing
    tasks: [task150, task151, task152, task153]
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "`kinnoo run` checks health of all declared services before executing the agent. Failed checks display service name, type, and actionable guidance."
      - id: AC2
        description: "HTTP health check performs a GET request to the declared URL and expects a 2xx status code. Timeout is 5 seconds (configurable)."
      - id: AC3
        description: "TCP health check attempts a socket connection to the declared port on localhost. Timeout is 3 seconds (configurable)."
      - id: AC4
        description: "Process health check verifies a process with the declared name is running."
      - id: AC5
        description: "In interactive mode, failed health checks produce a warning and prompt: 'Service <name> is not healthy. Proceed anyway? [y/N]'. In non-interactive mode, failed checks abort execution."
      - id: AC6
        description: "`kinnoo run --preflight` includes service health check results in its output alongside existing preflight checks."
      - id: AC7
        description: "Agents without declared services have no health check behavior — identical to V2 (no regression)."
      - id: AC8
        description: "Health check failures do not hard-block execution in interactive mode — the user can always proceed after the warning."
    notes:
      - "Depends on feature24 for schema; depends on feature14 for --preflight integration."
      - "Use stdlib `socket` for TCP checks, `urllib.request` for HTTP checks to avoid adding dependencies."
      - "Implement health checkers as a small interface (check method → pass/fail + message) in a dedicated module (src/kinnoo/health_check.py)."
    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature24, feature14]
    status: completed

  - id: feature27
    title: "Project Analyzer Module — Manifest Field Inference"
    description: |
      Add a reusable static analysis module (`src/kinnoo/analyzer.py`) that
      infers kinnoo manifest fields from an existing project directory. The
      analyzer is a detector-based engine used by `kinnoo import` and future
      onboarding workflows to minimize manual `kinnoo.yaml` authoring.

      Initial detectors:
      - `_detect_entrypoint`: infer entrypoint from common files and `__main__`.
      - `_detect_runtime`: infer language/version/type (one-shot vs mcp-server)
        and runtime port hints.
      - `_detect_framework`: infer framework from imports/usages.
      - `_detect_dependencies`: infer dependencies from requirements/pyproject.
      - `_detect_env_vars`: infer env vars from getenv/environ usage.
      - `_detect_assets`: infer bundle candidates from data/model artifacts.
      - `_detect_services`: infer likely external services and health-check hints.

      Analyzer output is structured with inferred values, per-field confidence,
      and warnings so callers can run a confirm-first UX.
    tasks: [task158, task159, task160, task161, task162]
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "A dedicated analyzer module exists (`src/kinnoo/analyzer.py`) with public API `analyze_project(project_dir) -> AnalysisReport` and detector helper functions."
      - id: AC2
        description: "Entrypoint/runtime/framework detection supports common Python agent layouts and emits confidence levels instead of hard failures when uncertain."
      - id: AC3
        description: "Dependency detection reads `requirements.txt` and `pyproject.toml` (project dependencies) and returns normalized package names/constraints."
      - id: AC4
        description: "Environment-variable detection scans source for `os.getenv`, `os.environ[...]`, and equivalent patterns, returning deduplicated env var names."
      - id: AC5
        description: "Asset detection identifies likely bundle candidates (for example `.npz`, `.onnx`, `.bin`, `.db`, model/data directories) with path-safety filtering."
      - id: AC6
        description: "Service detection emits suggested `services` entries based on recognizable connection patterns (for example redis/postgres/http endpoints) with health-check hints where possible."
      - id: AC7
        description: "Analyzer output includes three sections: inferred manifest fields, confidence metadata, and warnings/todo guidance for unresolved fields."
      - id: AC8
        description: "Analyzer is reusable by feature19 import flow without duplicating inference logic in command code."
      - id: AC9
        description: "Analyzer-only tests cover positive detection and uncertain/ambiguous cases for each detector; failures provide actionable diagnostics for debugging detector behavior."
    notes:
      - "Design constraint: detector functions should be independent and composable; each detector returns value + confidence + evidence string."
      - "Prefer stdlib parsing first (regex/ast/pathlib/tomllib); avoid heavyweight optional dependencies in the analyzer core."
      - "This feature is onboarding infrastructure and should be implemented before the full feature19 wizard UX."
      - "Deferred implementation planning lives in notes/tasks-todo-later.md and notes/tests-todo-later.md while feature23-feature26 are implemented first."

  - id: feature29
    title: "Remote Registry Server"
    description: |
      Implement a FastAPI-based registry server that stores agent archives in S3 and
      maintains a JSON metadata index. The server provides REST endpoints for the CLI
      client (feature28) to publish, install, search, and list agents. Authentication
      uses token-based auth for CLI and session-based auth for the web UI (feature29).

      Server endpoints:
        POST   /api/publish          — upload archive + metadata
        GET    /api/agents           — list all agents (paginated)
        GET    /api/agents/<name>    — get agent metadata + versions
        GET    /api/agents/<name>/<version>/download — presigned download URL
        GET    /api/search?q=<query> — search agents by name/description
        POST   /api/auth/token       — authenticate, get API token

      Metadata schema: name, version, description, author, checksum, upload_timestamp,
      archive_size_bytes.
    tasks: []
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: AC1
        description: "A FastAPI server application exists in a dedicated `server/` directory with proper project structure (requirements.txt, entry point)."
      - id: AC2
        description: "POST `/api/publish` accepts archive upload with metadata, stores archive in S3 (or S3-compatible storage), and updates JSON metadata index. Duplicate name+version returns 409 Conflict."
      - id: AC3
        description: "GET `/api/agents` returns paginated list of agents with metadata (name, latest version, description, author, archive size)."
      - id: AC4
        description: "GET `/api/agents/<name>/<version>/download` returns a presigned S3 download URL (archive is not proxied through the server)."
      - id: AC5
        description: "GET `/api/search?q=<query>` filters agents by name and description substring match."
      - id: AC6
        description: "POST `/api/auth/token` authenticates a user and returns an API token. All publish endpoints require valid token in Authorization header."
      - id: AC7
        description: "All endpoints return appropriate HTTP status codes (200, 201, 400, 401, 404, 409, 500) with JSON error bodies."
      - id: AC8
        description: "Server tests use FastAPI TestClient and mock S3 — no real AWS credentials required for testing."
    notes:
      - "This is a NEW server application, separate from the CLI package. Create under `server/` directory at project root."
      - "Use presigned URLs for archive upload/download to avoid proxying large files through the server."
      - "Keep metadata schema small: name, version, description, author, checksum, upload_timestamp, archive_size_bytes."
      - "Add pagination (offset/limit) to list and search endpoints from the start."
      - "S3 backend should be behind an abstraction layer for testing with local filesystem or moto."
      - "Server dependencies (fastapi, uvicorn, boto3) go in server/requirements.txt, NOT in the main kinnoo requirements.txt."
    owner: techlead-agent
    dependencies: [feature28]
    status: not-started

# This file contains a list of the tasks implemented by SWE agents - numbered task0, task1, task2, etc.
# Each new task should just increment the task number.
# The current task types are: 
#   - task: any general task to be implemented with code or through command(s)
#   - issue: anything that needs to be resolved - e.g., bug
#   - decision: any decision that needs to be made - e.g., choosing a model
#
# This file contains the project tasks as YAML entries. Use the top-level `tasks` list.
# Each task should reference its parent feature and list any test IDs it owns.
# The validator script `src/validate_project_manifests.py` will enforce unique IDs and references.
#
# Important Note: dependencies field can be other tasks, OR external packages, libraries, frameworks - with the version - that need to be installed in order to complete the task 
#
# Template (YAML):
# tasks:
#   - id: taskX
#     title: Short title
#     type: Task type (defaults to "task" if omitted)
#     description: Short description of the work
#     files: [path/to/file1, path/to/file2]
#     steps:
#       - Step 1 description
#       - Step 2 description
#     dependencies: [taskZ, boto3]
#     tests: [test0, test1]
#     status: not-started / in-progress / etc
#
# A decision task has different fields:
#
# Template for decision tasks (YAML):
# tasks:
#   - id: taskX
#     title: Short title
#     type: decision
#     description: Description of the decision to be made. Can include some initial choices, if available.
#     options: Potential choices for the decision (e.g., choice of model), as a YAML style list. Populated once these are available.
#           - option1: overview/pros/cons/artifacts
#           - option2: overview/pros/cons/artifacts
#     criteria: list of measurable evaluation criteria (latency, accuracy, size, license)
#     selected_option: option id (set when status: approved)
#     rationale: short reasoning for selection.
#     approvals: list of approvers: human name / agent ID (optional)
#     status: not-started / in-progress / etc
#
# Examples:
# tasks:
#   - id: task0
#     title: Add capture button to camera view
#     type: task
#     description: Add a white capture button centered at the bottom of the camera view and wire it to the capture action.
#     files: [Sources/Views/CameraView.swift]
#     steps:
#       - step1: Add SwiftUI button centered at the bottom of the camera view
#       - step2: Wire button action to `CameraViewModel.capturePhoto()`
#       - step3: Add unit/UI test verifying the button triggers the capture action
#     dependencies: []
#     tests: [test0]
#     status: not-started
#
#   - id: task10
#     title: Select CoreML model for waste classification
#     type: decision
#     description: Evaluate candidate CoreML models for on-device inference and choose one.
#     options:
#       - id: option1
#         name: MobileNetV2-quant
#         summary: Lightweight MobileNetV2 quantized
#         pros: [small size, fast inference]
#         cons: [lower accuracy on electronics class]
#         artifacts: [s3://models/mobilenetv2-quant.mlmodel]
#       - id: option2
#         name: EfficientNet-lite
#         summary: Better accuracy, slightly larger
#         pros: [higher accuracy]
#         cons: [bigger binary]
#         artifacts: [s3://models/efficientnet-lite.mlmodel]
#     criteria:
#       - latency_ms: "<=200"
#       - accuracy_top1: ">=0.80"
#       - size_mb: "<=20"
#     selected_option: option1
#     rationale: smaller size and faster inference time
#     approvals: []
#     status: completed

tasks:
  - id: task0
    title: Project structure and schema definition
    type: task
    description: |
      Create the kinnoo Python package structure and define the manifest schema
      as constants. Create the validate() function stub with the correct signature
      (is_valid: bool, errors: list[str]).
    files:
      - src/kinnoo/__init__.py
      - src/kinnoo/schema.py
      - src/kinnoo/validator.py
    steps:
      - step1: Create src/kinnoo/ package with __init__.py
      - step2: In schema.py, define REQUIRED_FIELDS list and FIELD_TYPES dict
      - step3: "In validator.py, create validate(manifest_path: str) -> tuple[bool, list[str]] stub"
      - step4: Add PyYAML to requirements.txt
    dependencies: []
    tests: [test4]
    status: completed

  - id: task1
    title: Required field and type validation
    type: task
    description: |
      Implement YAML parsing and validation for required fields and correct types.
      Return specific error messages naming the missing field or describing type mismatch.
    files:
      - src/kinnoo/validator.py
    steps:
      - step1: Parse YAML file using PyYAML
      - step2: Check each required field exists; collect errors for missing ones
      - step3: Check each field has correct type; collect errors for mismatches
      - step4: Return (False, errors) if any errors, (True, []) otherwise
    dependencies: [task0]
    tests: [test1, test2]
    status: completed

  - id: task2
    title: Semantic validation (semver, runtime.type, name format)
    type: task
    description: |
      Implement semantic validation: semver format for the version field,
      runtime.type must be "one-shot", name must be alphanumeric with hyphens only.
    files:
      - src/kinnoo/validator.py
    steps:
      - step1: Add semver regex validation for version field
      - step2: Add check that runtime.type == "one-shot"; error if not
      - step3: Add package name format validation (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$)
      - step4: Collect errors with descriptive messages for each violation
    dependencies: [task1]
    tests: [test3, test6]
    status: completed

  - id: task3
    title: Optional fields and integration
    type: task
    description: |
      Handle optional framework field (accept if present, ignore if absent).
      Ensure a fully valid manifest passes with no errors. Add docstrings and type hints.
    files:
      - src/kinnoo/validator.py
    steps:
      - step1: Ensure framework field does not trigger "missing field" error
      - step2: Ensure framework field with valid string value passes
      - step3: Verify complete valid manifest returns (True, [])
      - step4: Add docstrings and type hints to public API
    dependencies: [task2]
    tests: [test0, test5]
    status: completed

  - id: task4
    title: CLI entry point and argument parsing
    type: task
    description: |
      Create the kinnoo CLI entry point with argparse. Implement the `init` subcommand
      that parses the agent name argument. Handle missing arguments with clear usage message.
      Validate agent name format using NAME_PATTERN from schema.py.
    files:
      - src/kinnoo/cli.py
      - src/kinnoo/__init__.py
    steps:
      - step1: Create src/kinnoo/cli.py with argparse-based CLI structure
      - step2: Add `init` subcommand that accepts a positional `agent-name` argument
      - step3: "Print usage error if agent name is missing: 'Usage: kinnoo init <agent-name>'"
      - step4: Import NAME_PATTERN from schema.py and validate agent name; print error if invalid
      - step5: Add `kinnoo` console script entry point to pyproject.toml (create pyproject.toml if needed)
    dependencies: [task0]
    tests: [test7, test8, test15]
    status: completed

  - id: task5
    title: Template files and directory generation
    type: task
    description: |
      Create the scaffolding module that generates the agent directory structure
      with all template files. The generated kinnoo.yaml must pass feature1 validation.
      The run.py must include asyncio.run() boilerplate.
    files:
      - src/kinnoo/templates.py
      - src/kinnoo/init_command.py
    steps:
      - step1: Create src/kinnoo/templates.py with string templates for kinnoo.yaml, run.py, requirements.txt, README.md. requirements.txt template should be an empty file for MVP (no dependencies for hello-world agent)
      - step2: "kinnoo.yaml template: use agent name, version 0.1.0, entrypoint run.py, runtime python/>=3.10/one-shot, empty deps, inputs/outputs text"
      - step3: "run.py template: include asyncio.run() boilerplate with main(input_text) async function, print hello-world output"
      - step4: Create src/kinnoo/init_command.py with init_agent(name, target_dir) function
      - step5: Generate directory structure with tools/, prompts/ subdirectories
      - step6: Write all template files to the created directory
    dependencies: [task4]
    tests: [test9, test10, test11, test12]
    status: completed

  - id: task6
    title: Directory collision detection and CLI integration
    type: task
    description: |

    files:
      - src/kinnoo/init_command.py
      - src/kinnoo/cli.py
    steps:
      - step1: In init_command.py, check if target directory exists before creating
      - step2: "If exists, raise error or return failure: 'Error: Directory <name>/ already exists. Will not overwrite.'"
      - step3: Wire init_command.init_agent() into cli.py init subcommand handler
      - step4: Add integration test that runs full `kinnoo init` and verifies generated manifest passes validation
    dependencies: [task5]
    tests: [test13, test14]
    status: completed

Ensure the CLI handles corrupted/unreadable kinnoo.yaml and permission errors gracefully, always uses the validator for manifest checks, and does not modify files outside the agent directory.

      files in the agent directory excluding .venv/. Integrate into `kinnoo inspect` as a
      "Security sweep:" section and into `kinnoo pack` as a non-blocking warning.

      file.write(os.environ/os.getenv). Include disclaimer about false positives.
    files:

  - id: task116
    title: InputGuard protocol, result models, and factory function
    type: task
    description: |
      Create `src/kinnoo/input_guard.py` with the core architecture for the input safety
      guard system. Define result models (`InputGuardResult`, `InputWarning`), the
      `InputGuard` Protocol with two methods (`check` for single values and `check_inputs`
      for multi-value parameterized input), threat category constants, and the
      `get_default_guard()` factory function. This task establishes the pluggable contract:
      any class satisfying the Protocol can replace the regex guard (e.g., an ML classifier)
      by changing only the factory function.
    files:
      - src/kinnoo/input_guard.py
    steps:
      - 'step1: Create `src/kinnoo/input_guard.py`'
      - 'step2: Define `InputWarning` dataclass with fields: `threat_category: str`, `description: str`, `param_name: str | None = None`'
      - 'step3: Define `InputGuardResult` dataclass with fields: `safe: bool`, `warnings: list[InputWarning]`'
      - 'step4: Define threat category string constants: SQL_INJECTION, SHELL_INJECTION, PATH_TRAVERSAL, SSRF, XSS, TEMPLATE_INJECTION'
      - 'step5: Define `InputGuard` Protocol class with methods: `check(self, value: str, input_type: str = "text") -> InputGuardResult` and `check_inputs(self, inputs: list[tuple[str, str, str]]) -> InputGuardResult` where each tuple is (param_name, value, input_type)'
      - 'step6: Define `get_default_guard() -> InputGuard` factory function that returns `RegexInputGuard()` (placeholder class for now, fully implemented in task117)'
      - 'step7: Ensure the module is importable and `get_default_guard()` returns an instance with both `check` and `check_inputs` methods'
    dependencies: []
    tests: [test149, test150]
    status: completed

  - id: task117
    title: "RegexInputGuard — comprehensive injection pattern library"
    type: task
    description: |
      Implement the full `RegexInputGuard` class in `src/kinnoo/input_guard.py` with
      comprehensive regex patterns for 6 threat categories. Each pattern is a tuple of
      (compiled_regex, threat_category, human_description). The guard supports type-aware
      checking: different input_type values activate different pattern subsets. The
      `check_inputs()` method aggregates results across multiple typed parameters for
      future parameterized input support (-e, -i, -d, -u flags).

      Threat categories and patterns to implement:

      **SQL Injection** (SQL_INJECTION):
      - UNION SELECT / UNION ALL SELECT
      - DROP TABLE / DROP DATABASE
      - INSERT INTO ... VALUES
      - DELETE FROM
      - Tautology: OR 1=1, OR '1'='1', OR ''='', AND 1=1
      - Comment injection: --, #, /* (as SQL comment starters following injection context)
      - WAITFOR DELAY (time-based blind SQLi)
      - EXEC xp_ (stored procedure injection)
      - Stacked queries: semicolon followed by SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DROP

      **Shell Injection** (SHELL_INJECTION):
      - Command chaining: ; & | && || followed by dangerous commands (rm, cat, wget, curl,
        sudo, sh, bash, python, chmod, chown, nc, ncat, mkfifo, dd, kill)
      - Command substitution: $(...) and backtick `...`
      - Pipe to shell: | sh, | bash, | /bin/sh, | /bin/bash
      - Input/output redirection: > /etc/, >> /etc/, < /etc/
      - Null byte injection: \x00, %00

      **Path Traversal** (PATH_TRAVERSAL):
      - ../ and ..\ sequences (2+ levels)
      - URL-encoded variants: %2e%2e%2f, %2e%2e/, ..%2f
      - Double-encoding: %252e%252e%252f
      - Absolute sensitive paths: /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /proc/self, /dev/

      **SSRF** (SSRF):
      - Dangerous protocols: file://, gopher://, dict://, ldap://
      - Internal IPs: 127.0.0.1, 0.0.0.0, 10.x.x.x, 172.16-31.x.x, 192.168.x.x
      - IPv6 loopback: [::1], ::1 (as URL host)
      - localhost as hostname
      - Octal IP: 0177.0.0.1
      - AWS metadata endpoint: 169.254.169.254

      **XSS** (XSS):
      - <script tags (with variations like <ScRiPt, <script/src)
      - javascript: URI scheme
      - Event handlers: onerror=, onload=, onclick=, onmouseover=, onfocus=
      - Dangerous tags with event sources: <img, <iframe, <svg, <object, <embed
      - data:text/html

      **Template Injection** (TEMPLATE_INJECTION):
      - Jinja2/Twig: {{ and }}
      - ERB: <% and %>
      - Expression language: ${...}, #{...}

      **Type-aware input_type filtering:**
      - "text" or "string": all 6 categories
      - "file_path": PATH_TRAVERSAL + SHELL_INJECTION only
      - "url": SSRF + SHELL_INJECTION only
      - "id": SQL_INJECTION + SHELL_INJECTION + TEMPLATE_INJECTION only

      **check_inputs() multi-value aggregation:**
      - Iterate over (param_name, value, input_type) tuples
      - Call check(value, input_type) for each
      - Set param_name on each resulting InputWarning
      - Merge all warnings; safe = True only if all inputs are safe
    files:
      - src/kinnoo/input_guard.py
    steps:
      - 'step1: Define PATTERNS dict mapping threat category -> list of (regex_str, human_description) tuples'
      - 'step2: Define TYPE_FILTER dict mapping input_type -> set of applicable threat categories'
      - 'step3: Implement RegexInputGuard.check(value, input_type) — compile and match patterns filtered by input_type, return InputGuardResult with InputWarning for each match'
      - 'step4: Implement RegexInputGuard.check_inputs(inputs) — iterate over (param_name, value, input_type) tuples, aggregate results, set param_name on warnings'
      - 'step5: Add inline documentation for each pattern explaining what it catches and potential false positives'
      - 'step6: Ensure each pattern can be tested individually via the PATTERNS dict'
    dependencies: [task116]
    tests: [test151, test152, test153, test154, test155, test156, test157, test158, test159]
    status: completed

  - id: task118
    title: "CLI --no-guard flag and run_command integration"
    type: task
    description: |
      Add the `--no-guard` flag to the `kinnoo run` subcommand in cli.py and integrate
      the InputGuard into run_command.py. The guard runs after env var resolution but
      before entrypoint execution. When the guard flags input as unsafe, the user is
      warned and prompted to proceed. Non-interactive stdin (no TTY) auto-aborts as a
      fail-safe to prevent unattended execution of flagged input. The --no-guard flag
      skips the guard entirely for CI/automation pipelines.
    files:
      - src/kinnoo/cli.py
      - src/kinnoo/run_command.py
    steps:
      - 'step1: Add `--no-guard` argument to the run subparser in cli.py: `run_parser.add_argument("--no-guard", action="store_true", help="Disable input safety check")`'
      - 'step2: Pass `no_guard=bool(getattr(args, "no_guard", False))` to `run_agent()` call in cli.py'
      - 'step3: Add `no_guard: bool = False` parameter to `run_agent()` signature in run_command.py'
      - 'step4: In run_command.py, after env var resolution and before entrypoint execution, add guard integration block:
        - If not no_guard and input_arg is not None:
          - Import get_default_guard from input_guard
          - Call guard.check(input_arg, "text")
          - If not result.safe:
            - Print "[kinnoo] Input safety warning:" to stderr
            - For each warning, print "  - [{threat_category}] {description}" to stderr
            - If sys.stdin.isatty(): prompt "Proceed anyway? [y/N]: " and read response
            - If not sys.stdin.isatty() (non-interactive): print "Non-interactive mode: aborting." to stderr and return finalize(1)
            - If response is not "y" (case-insensitive): return finalize(1)
            - Handle KeyboardInterrupt and EOFError during prompt gracefully (abort with exit 1)'
      - 'step5: Ensure --no-guard bypasses the entire guard block (no import, no check, no prompt)'
      - 'step6: Ensure the guard does not run in preflight mode (preflight=True already returns early, but verify)'
    dependencies: [task117]
    tests: [test160, test161, test162, test163]
    status: completed

Omitting it keeps black-box behavior. This ensures backward compatibility and doesn't force framework adoption.\n\n## Notes on Framework Compatibility with &#96;python run.py&#96;\n\n### ⚠️ MVP: Async entrypoint template\n\nTwo of the top 5 frameworks (AutoGen, OpenAI Agents SDK) are async-first and require\n&#96;asyncio.run()&#96; boilerplate in the entrypoint script. The hello-world &#96;run.py&#96; template\ngenerated by &#96;kinnoo init&#96; should include this infrastructure by default — it is harmless\nfor synchronous agents (LangChain, CrewAI, smolagents) and required for async ones.\n\nRecommended default &#96;run.py&#96; template:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nimport sys\nimport asyncio\n\nasync def main(input_text: str) -&gt; str:\n    # Agent logic here\n    return \"Hello from your agent!\"\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    input_text = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) &gt; 1 else \"\"\n    result = asyncio.run(main(input_text))\n    print(result)\n\n## 🔮 V2+: MCP Server support\n\n### Background\nAs of early 2026, GitHub Copilot, Claude, Cursor, and others have adopted\n**Model Context Protocol (MCP)** as the universal standard for agent/tool extensibility.\nAn MCP server is a long-running process that exposes tools via structured JSON-RPC\nover stdin/stdout or HTTP — it is fundamentally different from a one-shot Python script.\n\nThis means MCP servers are **not** compatible with the MVP runtime contract\n(&#96;python run.py \"&lt;input&gt;\"&#96;), which assumes a one-shot execution model.\n\n### Why this matters for Kinnoo\nMCP is becoming the cross-platform tool standard. Supporting MCP server packages\nin Kinnoo would make the platform relevant to a much broader ecosystem — any developer\nbuilding tools for Copilot, Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, or other MCP-compatible clients\ncould use Kinnoo to package and distribute them.\n\n### What V2 support would require\n- A new manifest field: &#96;runtime.type: mcp-server&#96; (vs. the default &#96;runtime.type: one-shot&#96;)\n- A different execution model in the CLI: &#96;kinnoo run&#96; would launch the server as a\n  long-running process rather than invoking a one-shot script\n- A different entrypoint contract: the server listens on stdin/stdout or a local HTTP port\n  rather than accepting a CLI argument and printing to stdout\n\n### MVP stance\nMCP support is explicitly out of scope for MVP. The &#96;runtime.language&#96; and entrypoint\nfields in &#96;kinnoo.yaml&#96; are designed to be extensible to support this in V2 without\nbreaking the manifest schema.\n\n## 🔮 V2+: Manifest schema expansions\n\nThe following fields are **not** in scope for MVP. They are documented here for\nforward planning. All additions are designed to be additive — MVP manifests remain\nvalid in V2+.\n\n---\n\n### 1. Runtime type — long-running processes\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;yaml\nruntime:\n  language: python\n  version: \"&gt;=3.10\"\n  type: one-shot        # MVP — python run.py \"&lt;input&gt;\", process exits\n  # type: server        # Long-running HTTP server (FastAPI, Flask)\n  # type: mcp-server    # Long-running MCP protocol server (stdin/stdout or HTTP)\n  # type: worker        # Long-running background worker (queue consumer)\n  port: 8080            # Required when type: server or mcp-server\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nFor &#96;type: server&#96;, &#96;kinnoo run&#96; would launch the process and keep it alive.\nFor &#96;type: mcp-server&#96;, the CLI would handle the MCP handshake.\n\n---\n\n### 2. Memory / context\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;yaml\nmemory:\n  type: none            # MVP default — stateless\n  # type: in-process   # Agent manages state internally within a session\n  # type: vector        # External vector store (semantic search / RAG)\n  # type: key-value     # Simple persistent state (Redis, DynamoDB)\n  # type: episodic      # Conversation/episode history\n\n  # When type: vector or episodic:\n  backend: pinecone     # pinecone | chroma | weaviate | pgvector | qdrant\n  embedding_model: text-embedding-3-small\n  collection: my-agent-memory\n  retention_policy: 30d\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n### 3. Tools, MCP servers, databases\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;yaml\ntools:\n  - name: web_search\n    type: builtin         # Kinnoo-native tool\n\n  - name: github\n    type: mcp             # MCP server\n    server: github/github-mcp-server\n    version: \"&gt;=1.0.0\"\n    auth: env.GITHUB_TOKEN\n\n  - name: customer_db\n    type: database\n    engine: postgres\n    connection: env.DATABASE_URL\n    permissions:\n      - SELECT            # read-only for safety\n\n  - name: internal_api\n    type: http\n    base_url: https://api.internal.company.com\n    auth:\n      type: bearer\n      token: env.INTERNAL_API_KEY\n    endpoints:\n      - GET /orders/{id}\n      - POST /refunds\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n### 4. File store / RAG vector store\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;yaml\nstorage:\n  files:\n    - name: documents\n      type: local           # local | s3 | gcs | azure-blob\n      path: ./data/\n      permissions: read     # read | write | read-write\n\n    - name: output_store\n      type: s3\n      bucket: env.OUTPUT_BUCKET\n      prefix: agents/my-agent/outputs/\n      permissions: write\n\n  vector_stores:\n    - name: product_catalog\n      type: pinecone        # pinecone | chroma | weaviate | pgvector | qdrant\n      index: product-embeddings\n      embedding_model: text-embedding-3-small\n      connection: env.PINECONE_API_KEY\n      permissions: read\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n### Design principles for all V2+ fields\n\n- &#96;type:&#96; field on every block — keeps the schema extensible without breaking existing manifests\n- &#96;env.*&#96; references for all secrets — never hardcoded values\n- &#96;permissions:&#96; wherever the agent touches external systems — foundation for the future sandboxing/permission model\n- MVP fields remain unchanged — all V2+ fields are purely additive\n\n---\n\n## Agent Portability &amp; Sharing — Current State and Kinnoo Solution\n\n**Analysis Date:** 2026-02-18\n\n### Current State of Agent Sharing (2026)\n\n#### The Reality: Still Fragmented and Frustrating\n\n**Typical workflow today:**\n\n1. Clone repo\n2. Read README (if it exists)\n3. Figure out Python version, create venv\n4. &#96;pip install -r requirements.txt&#96; (pray for no conflicts)\n5. Hunt for required env vars / API keys\n6. Discover missing system tools (ffmpeg, poppler, etc.)\n7. Debug framework-specific config files\n8. Finally run... and hit a runtime error\n\n**Pain points by framework:**\n\n| Framework | Typical Friction |\n|-----------|------------------|\n| LangChain | Heavy deps, version sensitivity, config spread across files |\n| CrewAI | Crew/agent YAML configs, role definitions, tool wiring |\n| AutoGen | Async setup, conversation patterns, multi-agent orchestration |\n\n**What makes sharing hard today:**\n- No standard manifest → every repo is a snowflake\n- No standard entrypoint → &#96;main.py&#96;? &#96;run.py&#96;? &#96;agent.py&#96;? &#96;python -m agent&#96;?\n- Implicit dependencies → \"oh you need Redis running\" buried in code\n- API key management → scattered .env patterns, no validation\n- Framework lock-in → CrewAI agent can't easily run LangChain tools\n\n---\n\n### How Kinnoo Solves This\n\n#### Core Insight\n\nThe problem isn't technical complexity—it's **lack of convention**. Kinnoo provides:\n\n1. **Standard manifest** → predictable metadata\n2. **Standard entrypoint** → &#96;python run.py \"&lt;input&gt;\"&#96;\n3. **Bundled dependencies** → reproducible installs\n4. **Declarative requirements** → explicit runtime needs\n\n#### Solving Runtime Assumptions (Pragmatic Approach)\n\n**Not complicated. Here's the plan:**\n\n##### Layer 1: Declare It (Manifest Extensions)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;yaml\n# filepath: kinnoo.yaml\nname: my-agent\nversion: 1.0.0\nentrypoint: run.py\n\n# New fields (simple additions)\nruntime:\n  python: \"3.11\"\n  \ntools:\n  - name: ffmpeg\n    required: false\n  - name: tesseract\n    required: true\n\nservices:\n  - name: redis\n    mock: true  # kinnoo can provide a mock\n\nresources:\n  gpu: optional  # or \"required\" or \"none\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Implementation effort:** Extend existing schema validator. ~1-2 tasks.\n\n##### Layer 2: Check It (Preflight)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n$ kinnoo run my-agent --preflight\n\n✓ Python 3.11 found\n✓ ffmpeg found (optional)\n✗ tesseract not found (required)\n  → Fix: brew install tesseract\n✓ redis mock available\n✓ GPU not required\n&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Implementation:** Simple Python checks using &#96;shutil.which()&#96;, &#96;subprocess&#96;, &#96;platform&#96;. ~2-3 tasks.\n\n##### Layer 3: Bundle It (Wheel Cache)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n$ kinnoo pack\n\nDownloading wheels for platform: macosx_arm64\nBundling 47 packages into my-agent-1.0.0.kno\n&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Implementation:** Use &#96;pip wheel&#96; + &#96;pip download&#96;. Store in archive. Install with &#96;pip install --find-links&#96;. ~2-3 tasks.\n\n##### Layer 4: Mock It (Service Stubs)\n\nFor common services, provide drop-in mocks:\n\n| Service | Kinnoo Mock |\n|---------|-------------|\n| Redis | &#96;fakeredis&#96; (pure Python) |\n| PostgreSQL | SQLite with compatibility shim |\n| S3 | &#96;moto&#96; or local filesystem |\n\n**Implementation:** Ship a small &#96;kinnoo.mocks&#96; module with these. Inject via env vars. ~3-4 tasks.\n\n##### Layer 5: Escape Hatch (Docker/Remote)\n\nWhen local won't work:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n$ kinnoo run my-agent --docker    # Use bundled Dockerfile\n$ kinnoo run my-agent --remote    # Send to configured runner\n&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Implementation:** Generate Dockerfile from manifest. Remote runner is V2+. ~2-3 tasks for Docker.\n\n---\n\n### Complexity Assessment\n\n| Component | Effort | Builds On |\n|-----------|--------|-----------|\n| Manifest extensions | Low | Existing schema (feature1) |\n| Preflight checker | Low | stdlib: shutil, subprocess, platform |\n| Wheel bundling | Medium | pip wheel, pip download |\n| Service mocks | Medium | Existing libs: fakeredis, moto |\n| Docker generation | Low | Template Dockerfile from manifest |\n| Remote runner | Higher | Defer to V2 |\n\n**Total for MVP portability:** ~10-15 tasks, spread across 2-3 features\n\n**For a Senior Engineer with AI agent assistance:** Very doable. You're orchestrating existing tools, not building from scratch.\n\n---\n\n### What Makes Kinnoo Unique (vs \"just use Docker\")\n\n| Docker Approach | Kinnoo Approach |\n|-----------------|-----------------|\n| Heavy images (GB) | Lightweight bundles (MB) |\n| Requires Docker installed | Native Python, Docker optional |\n| Opaque blob | Inspectable manifest + wheels |\n| All-or-nothing isolation | Graduated: venv → sandbox → container |\n| Slow iteration | Fast local runs |\n| Hard to customize | Easy to extend/mock |\n\n**Kinnoo philosophy:** Docker is an escape hatch, not the default. Most agents don't need full containerization—they need reproducible Python environments with clear contracts.\n\n---\n\n### Recommended Roadmap\n\n**MVP (Features 1-5):**\n- Manifest with runtime/tools/services fields\n- Preflight checker with actionable output\n- Wheel bundling in &#96;.kno&#96; archive\n- Basic service mocks (redis, sqlite-as-postgres)\n\n**V1.1:**\n- Dockerfile generation from manifest\n- GPU detection and warnings\n- Tool auto-install suggestions\n\n**V2:**\n- Remote runner for GPU/heavy workloads\n- Framework adapters (LangChain, CrewAI templates)\n- Registry with capability filtering\n\n---\n\n### Summary\n\n| Question | Answer |\n|----------|--------|\n| Is sharing agents hard today? | Yes—no conventions, implicit deps, framework sprawl |\n| Can kinnoo solve this? | Yes—standard manifest + entrypoint + bundling |\n| Is it complicated to build? | No—mostly glue code over existing tools |\n| Doable for Senior Engineer + AI? | Absolutely—10-15 focused tasks |\n\nThe hard part isn't the code—it's the design decisions. You've already made the key ones (black-box execution, framework-agnostic MVP, declarative manifest). Implementation is straightforward integration work.\n\n---\n\n## Packaging Kinnoo for Pip Installation — MVP Requirement\n\n**Decision Date:** 2026-02-18  \n**Status:** **Required for MVP** (likely the final feature)  \n**Context:** User feedback\n\n### Problem Statement\n\n**Q: How would a user install &#96;kinnoo&#96;?**  \n**A:** The most common way to install Python packages like &#96;kinnoo&#96; is via &#96;pip&#96;. This requires packaging the project as a Python package and making it available through either:\n- **PyPI** (Python Package Index) — public registry, &#96;pip install kinnoo&#96;\n- **Git repository** — direct install, &#96;pip install git+https://github.com/username/kinnoo.git&#96;\n\n### Why This Must Be Part of the MVP\n\n**Core principle:** If kinnoo is a tool for making agents easy to install and run, then **kinnoo itself must be easy to install and run.**\n\nWithout proper packaging:\n- Other developers can't easily try kinnoo\n- Installation requires manual cloning, venv setup, dependency installation\n- No version management or updates\n- Violates the \"batteries included\" philosophy\n\n### Current State\n\nThe groundwork is already in place:\n- ✅ &#96;pyproject.toml&#96; exists in the project\n- ✅ Package structure already set up (&#96;src/kinnoo/&#96;)\n- ✅ Console script entry point already specified (task4 for feature2)\n\n### What's Required (Implementation Plan)\n\n#### 1. Complete &#96;pyproject.toml&#96; Metadata\n\nAdd the necessary metadata fields:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;toml\n[project]\nname = \"kinnoo\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"  # Start with MVP version\ndescription = \"A lightweight package manager for AI agents\"\nreadme = \"README.md\"\nrequires-python = \"&gt;=3.10\"\nlicense = {text = \"MIT\"}  # or appropriate license\nauthors = [\n    {name = \"Your Name\", email = \"your.email@example.com\"}\n]\nkeywords = [\"ai\", \"agents\", \"packaging\", \"cli\"]\nclassifiers = [\n    \"Development Status :: 3 - Alpha\",\n    \"Intended Audience :: Developers\",\n    \"License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License\",\n    \"Programming Language :: Python :: 3\",\n    \"Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10\",\n    \"Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11\",\n    \"Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12\",\n]\n\n[project.urls]\nHomepage = \"https://github.com/username/kinnoo\"\nRepository = \"https://github.com/username/kinnoo\"\nIssues = \"https://github.com/username/kinnoo/issues\"\n\ndependencies = [\n    \"PyYAML&gt;=6.0\",\n]\n\n[project.optional-dependencies]\ndev = [\n    \"pytest&gt;=7.0\",\n]\n\n[project.scripts]\nkinnoo = \"kinnoo.cli:main\"\n\n[build-system]\nrequires = [\"setuptools&gt;=61.0\", \"wheel\"]\nbuild-backend = \"setuptools.build_meta\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### 2. Test Local Installation\n\nBefore publishing, verify the package installs correctly:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Build the package\npython3 -m build\n\n# Install locally from the built wheel\npip install dist/kinnoo-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl\n\n# Test the CLI\nkinnoo --help\nkinnoo init test-agent\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### 3. Build and Share Wheel Files (MVP Distribution Method)\n\n**Strategy:** Start simple—build wheels and share directly with early users.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Build the package\npython3 -m build\n\n# This creates dist/kinnoo-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl\n# Share this file with early users via email, Slack, Dropbox, etc.\n\n# Users install locally:\npip install kinnoo-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Pros:**\n- ✅ **Simplest possible distribution** — no servers, no infrastructure\n- ✅ **Complete privacy** — only people you explicitly send the file to can install\n- ✅ **No Git access needed** — just a .whl file\n- ✅ **Fast iteration** — build and share new versions instantly\n- ✅ **Perfect for MVP validation** — get feedback before investing in infrastructure\n\n**Cons:**\n- Manual distribution (acceptable for small group of early users)\n- No automatic updates (users install new .whl files manually)\n- Not scalable beyond ~10-20 users\n\n**Privacy considerations:**\n- ✅ **Maximum privacy** — you control exactly who gets the file\n- ✅ **No public exposure** — not indexed by AI bots or search engines\n- ✅ **No Git repo needed** — can even work with completely private/local development\n\n#### 4. Private Git-Based Installation (Post-V2, For Scaling Private Testing)\n\n**Deferred to post-V2** when ready to scale beyond direct file sharing:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Invited collaborators with repo access can install:\npip install git+https://github.com/username/kinnoo.git@v0.2.0\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis requires:\n- Private Git repository with controlled access\n- Access control via GitHub collaborators/teams\n- Users need Git access (SSH keys or tokens)\n\n**When to transition:** When manual wheel sharing becomes cumbersome (~10-20+ users), or when you want automatic version tracking.\n\nAlternative: **GitHub Packages** (PyPI-compatible private hosting)\n\n#### 5. Public PyPI Publication (V3/V4+, After Product-Market Fit)\n\n**Deferred to V3/V4+** when kinnoo has achieved product-market fit with private users:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Build distribution packages\npython3 -m build\n\n# Upload to public PyPI (makes it publicly accessible)\npython3 -m twine upload dist/*\n\n# Anyone can then install:\npip install kinnoo\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n⚠️ **PyPI is completely public** — only publish when ready for full public release.\n\nOptional pre-release testing with **TestPyPI**:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\npython3 -m twine upload --repository testpypi dist/*\npip install --index-url https://test.pypi.org/simple/ kinnoo\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Recommended Approach for MVP\n\n**MVP (Private Wheel Distribution):**\n1. Complete &#96;pyproject.toml&#96; metadata\n2. Test local installation (&#96;pip install .&#96;)\n3. Build wheel: &#96;python3 -m build&#96;\n4. Test wheel installation: &#96;pip install dist/kinnoo-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl&#96;\n5. Document wheel installation in README.md\n6. Share .whl file directly with early users (email, Slack, etc.)\n\n**Post-V2 (Scale Private Distribution):**\n7. Set up private GitHub repo (if not already)\n8. Test Git-based installation\n9. Document Git installation method\n10. Transition users to Git-based installs\n11. Alternative: Consider GitHub Packages for PyPI-like private hosting\n\n**V3/V4+ (Public Release, After Product-Market Fit):**\n12. Optional: Test on TestPyPI first\n13. Publish to public PyPI\n14. Update README with &#96;pip install kinnoo&#96;\n15. Public announcement\n\n### Implementation Effort\n\n| Task | Effort | Priority | Phase |\n|------|--------|----------|-------|\n| Complete pyproject.toml metadata | Low (1 task) | **Required** | MVP |\n| Test local installation (&#96;pip install .&#96;) | Low (validation) | **Required** | MVP |\n| Build wheel (&#96;python3 -m build&#96;) | Low (validation) | **Required** | MVP |\n| Test wheel installation | Low (validation) | **Required** | MVP |\n| Update README with wheel install instructions | Low (documentation) | **Required** | MVP |\n| Set up Git-based installation | Low (validation) | Optional | Post-V2 |\n| GitHub Packages setup | Medium (1-2 tasks) | Optional | Post-V2 |\n| Publish to TestPyPI | Medium (1-2 tasks) | Optional | V3/V4+ |\n| Publish to public PyPI | Medium (1-2 tasks) | Deferred | V3/V4+ |\n\n**Total MVP effort:** 2-3 tasks for wheel-based distribution\n\n### Where This Fits in the MVP\n\n**Recommendation:** Make this the **last feature** before declaring MVP complete.\n\n**Rationale:**\n1. All other features (manifest validation, init, run, list, etc.) must be implemented first\n2. Packaging is the final step that proves kinnoo is ready for users\n3. Enables dogfooding—use kinnoo to package kinnoo\n4. Natural completion milestone—\"kinnoo can now be distributed as a wheel\"\n5. Maximum privacy for early validation—you control exactly who gets access\n6. Simple to scale up later (Git → PyPI) as project matures\n\n### Success Criteria\n\n**MVP (Wheel Distribution):**\n\nWhen complete, you should be able to:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Build kinnoo\npython3 -m build\n\n# Install and test locally\npip install dist/kinnoo-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl\nkinnoo --version\nkinnoo init my-agent\ncd my-agent\nkinnoo run \"Hello, world!\"\n\n# Share with early users\n# They can install the same way:\npip install kinnoo-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Post-V2 (Git-Based Distribution, When Scaling):**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Users with repo access install:\npip install git+https://github.com/username/kinnoo.git@v0.2.0\n\n# Same commands work\nkinnoo --version\nkinnoo init my-agent\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**V3/V4+ (Public PyPI, After Product-Market Fit):**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Public installation\npip install kinnoo\n\n# Same commands work\nkinnoo --version\nkinnoo init my-agent\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Distribution Strategy Summary\n\n| Phase | Method | Target Audience | Privacy Level |\n|-------|--------|-----------------|---------------|\n| **MVP** | **Wheel files** | Early testers (1-10) | **Maximum** — you control file sharing |\n| Post-V2 | Git-based or GitHub Packages | Private beta (10-100) | High — invite-only via repo access |\n| V3/V4+ | Public PyPI | General public | Public — anyone can install |\n\n**This is essential for the MVP vision: making AI agents as easy to install as any other Python package, while starting with the simplest distribution method and maintaining maximum privacy during early validation.**\n\n---\n\n## V2 Strategy: LangChain Adapter + MCP Server Integration\n\n**Decision Date:** 2026-02-18  \n**Status:** Planned (post-MVP)  \n**Scope:** V2\n\n### V2 Goal\n\n**One framework, done extremely well, with real tool support.**\n\nEnable a LangChain developer to package an agent that uses MCP tools, share it, and have another developer run it with minimal friction.\n\n### Why LangChain First?\n\n- Largest community (most users to validate with)\n- Most documentation/examples\n- LangChain has native MCP support\n- If kinnoo works for LangChain, others will ask for their framework\n- Demand-driven expansion &gt; speculative expansion\n\n### MCP Support Levels\n\n| Level | What | V2? | Complexity |\n|-------|------|-----|------------|\n| **Declare** | List MCP servers in manifest | ✅ Yes | Low |\n| **Verify** | Preflight checks (\"is this server available?\") | ✅ Yes | Low |\n| **Launch** | &#96;kinnoo run&#96; starts required MCP servers | ✅ Yes | Medium |\n| **Bundle** | Package MCP server binaries into .kno | ❌ V3+ | High |\n\n**V2 Scope:** Declare + Verify + Launch (not Bundle)\n\n### MCP Manifest Schema\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;yaml\n# kinnoo.yaml\nname: my-research-agent\nversion: 1.0.0\nframework: langchain\n\nmcp_servers:\n  - name: filesystem\n    package: \"@anthropics/mcp-filesystem\"  # npm package\n    config:\n      allowed_directories:\n        - \"./data\"\n    required: true\n    \n  - name: brave-search\n    package: \"@anthropics/mcp-brave-search\"\n    config:\n      api_key: env.BRAVE_API_KEY\n    required: true\n    \n  - name: github\n    package: \"@anthropics/mcp-github\"\n    config:\n      token: env.GITHUB_TOKEN\n    required: false  # optional tool\n    \n  - name: postgres\n    package: \"@anthropics/mcp-postgres\"\n    config:\n      connection_string: env.DATABASE_URL\n    required: false\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### What &#96;kinnoo run&#96; Does in V2\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n$ kinnoo run my-agent \"research topic X\"\n\nPreflight checks:\n✓ Python 3.11 found\n✓ Node.js/npx available\n✓ MCP server: filesystem (npx @anthropics/mcp-filesystem)\n✓ MCP server: brave-search (npx @anthropics/mcp-brave-search)\n  → BRAVE_API_KEY set\n✗ MCP server: github (optional, skipping)\n  → GITHUB_TOKEN not set\n\nStarting MCP servers...\n✓ filesystem listening on stdio\n✓ brave-search listening on stdio\n\nRunning agent...\n[agent output]\n\nShutting down MCP servers...\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Why This Works\n\n1. **Most MCP servers are npm packages** → &#96;npx @anthropics/mcp-xxx&#96; just works\n2. **Stdio-based** → No port management, just spawn processes\n3. **Config is declarative** → User fills in env vars, kinnoo wires it up\n4. **Credentials via env** → No secrets in manifest, standard pattern\n5. **LangChain has MCP support** → Native integration, no custom wiring\n\n### Supported MCP Servers (V2 Initial Set)\n\nFocus on stable, well-documented npm packages:\n\n| Server | Package | Use Case |\n|--------|---------|----------|\n| Filesystem | &#96;@anthropics/mcp-filesystem&#96; | Read/write local files |\n| Brave Search | &#96;@anthropics/mcp-brave-search&#96; | Web search |\n| GitHub | &#96;@anthropics/mcp-github&#96; | Repo operations |\n| Postgres | &#96;@anthropics/mcp-postgres&#96; | Database queries |\n| Supabase | &#96;@supabase/mcp-server&#96; | Supabase integration |\n| SQLite | &#96;@anthropics/mcp-sqlite&#96; | Local database |\n\n### What We're NOT Doing in V2\n\n- **Bundling server binaries** → User must have npx/node installed (acceptable)\n- **Custom MCP servers** → Only well-known packages with stable APIs\n- **HTTP-based MCP servers** → Stdio only (simpler lifecycle)\n- **Server versioning/pinning** → Use latest (add pinning in V3)\n- **Memory abstraction** → Too complex, framework-specific (defer to V3)\n- **Other framework adapters** → CrewAI, AutoGen, etc. deferred to V3\n\n### V2 Developer Workflow\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Create agent with LangChain + MCP tools\nkinnoo init my-agent --framework=langchain --mcp=filesystem,brave-search\n\n# Edit agent logic, configure API keys in .env\ncd my-agent &amp;&amp; edit...\n\n# Run with MCP servers auto-launched\nkinnoo run . \"search for X and save to ./data/results.txt\"\n# → Starts filesystem + brave-search MCP servers\n# → Runs agent\n# → Agent uses tools\n# → Shuts down servers\n\n# Package and share\nkinnoo pack\n# → my-agent.kno includes manifest with MCP requirements\n\n# Recipient\nkinnoo install my-agent.kno\n# Preflight warns: \"This agent requires BRAVE_API_KEY, Node.js\"\nkinnoo run my-agent \"query\"\n# → Same MCP server launch flow\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### V2 Implementation Estimate\n\n| Task | Effort | Notes |\n|------|--------|-------|\n| &#96;framework&#96; manifest field | Low | Schema extension |\n| &#96;mcp_servers&#96; manifest field | Low | Schema extension |\n| &#96;kinnoo init --framework=langchain&#96; | Medium | LangChain-specific scaffold |\n| &#96;kinnoo init --mcp=...&#96; flag | Medium | MCP server config templates |\n| MCP server preflight checks | Low | &#96;which npx&#96;, env var checks |\n| MCP server launcher/lifecycle | Medium | Spawn processes, manage stdio |\n| Wire to LangChain MCP client | Medium | LangChain has MCP support |\n| Common server config templates | Low | 5-6 server configs |\n| Documentation | Medium | User guide for LangChain + MCP |\n\n**Total V2 effort:** ~8-12 tasks (4-6 weeks with AI assistance)\n\n### V3+ Roadmap (Deferred)\n\n| Feature | Why Deferred |\n|---------|--------------|\n| CrewAI adapter | Wait for V2 LangChain validation |\n| AutoGen adapter | Wait for V2 LangChain validation |\n| MCP server bundling | Complex; requires Node.js packaging |\n| Memory abstraction | Framework-specific, needs research |\n| Server version pinning | Wait for ecosystem to stabilize |\n| HTTP MCP servers | More complex lifecycle management |\n\n### Success Criteria for V2\n\nWhen complete, this workflow should work end-to-end:\n\n1. Developer A creates LangChain agent with MCP tools\n2. Developer A runs &#96;kinnoo pack&#96; → gets &#96;.kno&#96; file\n3. Developer A shares &#96;.kno&#96; file with Developer B\n4. Developer B runs &#96;kinnoo install&#96; + &#96;kinnoo run&#96;\n5. MCP servers launch automatically\n6. Agent executes with tools working\n7. Developer B did not need to understand MCP, LangChain internals, or manual setup\n\n**Key metric:** Time from receiving &#96;.kno&#96; to running agent &lt; 5 minutes (assuming deps installed).\n\n### Possible additional frameworks to support for V2\n\nHere are some **single-agent frameworks** that would be relatively easy to support in kinnoo V2 (after LangChain and possibly LlamaIndex):\n\n---\n\n### 1. **LlamaIndex**\n- **Why easy:** Pythonic, simple agent API, minimal dependencies, similar entrypoint pattern to LangChain.\n- **What’s needed:** Template with &#96;llama_index&#96; in &#96;requirements.txt&#96;, example agent in &#96;main.py&#96;.\n\n---\n\n### 2. **Haystack**\n- **Why easy:** Well-documented, supports pipeline/agent pattern, can expose a simple &#96;run(input)&#96; interface.\n- **What’s needed:** Template with &#96;haystack&#96; in &#96;requirements.txt&#96;, example pipeline/agent in &#96;main.py&#96;.\n\n---\n\n### 3. **Semantic Kernel (Python)**\n- **Why easy:** Has a Python SDK, supports function calling and skills, can be wrapped in a simple entrypoint.\n- **What’s needed:** Template with &#96;semantic-kernel&#96; in &#96;requirements.txt&#96;, example kernel in &#96;main.py&#96;.\n\n---\n\n### 4. **AutoGPT (as a library)**\n- **Why easy:** Recent versions can be used as a Python package, can expose a single-agent workflow.\n- **What’s needed:** Template with &#96;autogpt&#96; in &#96;requirements.txt&#96;, example agent in &#96;main.py&#96;.\n\n---\n\n### 5. **OpenAI Function Calling (barebones)**\n- **Why easy:** Just needs &#96;openai&#96; package, a prompt, and a function call handler.\n- **What’s needed:** Template with &#96;openai&#96; in &#96;requirements.txt&#96;, example function-calling agent in &#96;main.py&#96;.\n\n---\n\n**Summary:**  \nLlamaIndex and Haystack are the easiest after LangChain, as they have clear agent APIs and minimal setup.  \nSemantic Kernel and barebones OpenAI function-calling are also straightforward.  \nChoose frameworks with simple, well-documented APIs and minimal external dependencies for the smoothest V2 integration.\nMulti-Agent (LangGraph, CrewAI) is harder\n\n---\n\n## Onboarding Existing Agents — Q&amp;A (2026-03-01)\n\nGreat questions. You’re focusing on exactly the right onboarding friction points.\n\n**1) Existing LangChain agent → package with kinnoo pack**\n- Keep your existing project; you do not need to rewrite it for Kinnoo.\n- Ensure there is a single runnable entrypoint that accepts one input argument and prints output.\n- Ensure requirements.txt lists your dependencies.\n- Add kinnoo.yaml (or bootstrap it with kinnoo init and adapt it).\n- Verify locally with kinnoo run path/to/agent \"test input\".\n- Package with kinnoo pack path/to/agent.\n- Result: a .kno archive that others can install/run.\n\n**2) Do they need to write kinnoo.yaml manually?**\n- Not strictly.
